title: Anne of Green Gables
author: Lucy Maud Montgomery
description: 《绿山墙的安妮》是加拿大著名女作家露西·莫德·蒙哥马利于 1908 年出版的享誉世界的儿童与成长文学至高名篇。本文件收录了全书完整的 38 个章节。故事讲述了绿山墙农场的马修与玛丽拉兄妹本想领养一个男孩帮忙做农活，却阴差阳错迎来了一个满头红发、喋喋不休却拥有丰富想象力的孤儿女孩安妮·雪莉。安妮凭借她的纯真、热情、乐观与惊人的才华，不仅赢得了马修与玛丽拉深沉的爱，还收获了与戴安娜的至真友情以及与吉尔伯特的深厚情谊，最终在爱与成长中成长为一名出色的女性。

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is Surprised
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 1 章：雷切尔·林德太太的惊奇发现

paragraphs.en: MRS. Rachel Lynde lived just where the Avonlea main road dipped down into a little hollow, fringed with alders and ladies’ eardrops and traversed by a brook that had its source away back in the woods of the old Cuthbert place; it was reputed to be an intricate, headlong brook in its earlier course through those woods, with dark secrets of pool and cascade; but by the time it reached Lynde’s Hollow it was a quiet, well-conducted little stream, for not even a brook could run past Mrs. Rachel Lynde’s door without due regard for decency and decorum; it probably was conscious that Mrs. Rachel was sitting at her window, keeping a sharp eye on everything that passed, from brooks and children up, and that if she noticed anything odd or out of place she would never rest until she had ferreted out the whys and wherefores thereof.
paragraphs.zh: 太太。雷切尔·林德住的地方就在埃文利主干道伸入一个小洼地的地方，周围种满了桤木和女士耳坠，一条小溪流过，小溪的源头就在老卡斯伯特家的树林里。据说，它是一条复杂的、急速流过树林的小溪，其中有水池和瀑布的黑暗秘密。但当它到达林德山谷时，它是一条安静的、疏导良好的小溪，因为即使是一条小溪也不能流过雷切尔·林德太太的门，而不考虑体面和礼节。雷切尔夫人可能意识到，她正坐在窗前，敏锐地观察着从溪流到孩子们的一切经过，如果她发现任何奇怪或不合适的地方，她永远不会休息，直到她找出其中的原因和原因。

paragraphs.en: With this Mrs. Rachel stepped out of the lane into the backyard of Green Gables. Very green and neat and precise was that yard, set about on one side with great patriarchal willows and on the other with prim Lombardies. Not a stray stick nor stone was to be seen, for Mrs. Rachel would have seen it if there had been. Privately she was of the opinion that Marilla Cuthbert swept that yard over as often as she swept her house. One could have eaten a meal off the ground without overbrimming the proverbial peck of dirt.
paragraphs.zh: 说完，雷切尔夫人走出小巷，来到绿山墙的后院。那个院子绿油油的，整洁而精确，一侧种着父权制的大柳树，另一侧种着古板的伦巴第人。没有看到一根杂乱的棍子或石头，因为如果有的话，雷切尔夫人一定会看到的。私下里，她认为玛丽拉·卡斯伯特打扫那个院子的次数和打扫她房子的次数一样多。人们可以在地上吃一顿饭，而不会沾满众所周知的泥土。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, no, I’m quite well although I had a bad headache yesterday,” she said. “Matthew went to Bright River. We’re getting a little boy from an orphan asylum in Nova Scotia and he’s coming on the train tonight.” If Marilla had said that Matthew had gone to Bright River to meet a kangaroo from Australia Mrs. Rachel could not have been more astonished. She was actually stricken dumb for five seconds. It was unsupposable that Marilla was making fun of her, but Mrs. Rachel was almost forced to suppose it. “Are you in earnest, Marilla?” she demanded when voice returned to her. “Yes, of course,” said Marilla, as if getting boys from orphan asylums in Nova Scotia were part of the usual spring work on any well-regulated Avonlea farm instead of being an unheard of innovation.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，不，虽然我昨天头痛得很厉害，但我很好，”她说。 “马修去了布赖特河。我们从新斯科舍省的一家孤儿院接收了一个小男孩，他今晚要乘火车来。”如果玛丽拉说马修去布赖特河去见一只来自澳大利亚的袋鼠，雷切尔夫人一定会感到更加惊讶。她竟然愣了五秒钟。玛丽拉不可能取笑她，但雷切尔夫人几乎不得不这么认为。 “你是认真的吗，玛丽拉？”当声音恢复时，她问道。 “是的，当然，”玛丽拉说，仿佛从新斯科舍省的孤儿院接收男孩是任何管理良好的埃文利农场春季工作的一部分，而不是闻所未闻的创新。

paragraphs.en: “Well, Marilla, I’ll just tell you plain that I think you’re doing a mighty foolish thing--a risky thing, that’s what. You don’t know what you’re getting. You’re bringing a strange child into your house and home and you don’t know a single thing about him nor what his disposition is like nor what sort of parents he had nor how he’s likely to turn out. Why, it was only last week I read in the paper how a man and his wife up west of the Island took a boy out of an orphan asylum and he set fire to the house at night--set it on purpose, Marilla--and nearly burnt them to a crisp in their beds. And I know another case where an adopted boy used to suck the eggs--they couldn’t break him of it. If you had asked my advice in the matter--which you didn’t do, Marilla--I’d have said for mercy’s sake not to think of such a thing, that’s what.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，玛丽拉，我就直截了当地告诉你，我认为你正在做一件非常愚蠢的事情——一件冒险的事情，就是这样。你不知道你会得到什么。你把一个陌生的孩子带进你的房子和家里，你对他一无所知，也不知道他的性格是什么样的，也不知道他有什么样的父母，也不知道他可能会变成什么样子。哎呀，就在上周，我在报纸上读到，一对男人和他的妻子在西边岛从孤儿院带了一个男孩，晚上放火烧了房子——玛丽拉，是故意的——差点把他们在床上烧成碎片。我知道另一个例子，一个被收养的男孩经常吸鸡蛋——如果你在这件事上征求了我的意见——但你没有这样做，玛丽拉——我会说看在仁慈的份上不要考虑这样的事情，就是这样。”

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Matthew Cuthbert is Surprised
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 2 章：马修·卡斯伯特的意外震惊

paragraphs.en: MATTHEW Cuthbert and the sorrel mare jogged comfortably over the eight miles to Bright River. It was a pretty road, running along between snug farmsteads, with now and again a bit of balsamy fir wood to drive through or a hollow where wild plums hung out their filmy bloom. The air was sweet with the breath of many apple orchards and the meadows sloped away in the distance to horizon mists of pearl and purple; while “The little birds sang as if it were The one day of summer in all the year.” Matthew enjoyed the drive after his own fashion, except during the moments when he met women and had to nod to them--for in Prince Edward Island you are supposed to nod to all and sundry you meet on the road whether you know them or not.
paragraphs.zh: 马修·卡斯伯特和栗色母马轻松地慢跑了八英里，到达了布赖特河。这是一条漂亮的路，沿着舒适的农庄蜿蜒而行，时不时可以驶过一些香脂杉木，或者是一个空地，那里野李子挂着薄薄的花朵。空气中弥漫着许多苹果园的芳香，草地在远处倾斜，一直延伸到地平线上的珍珠色和紫色的薄雾。而“小鸟们歌唱着，仿佛这是一年中夏天的一天。”马修按照自己的方式享受开车的乐趣，除了在他遇到女人并不得不向她们点头的那一刻之外——因为在爱德华王子岛，你应该向路上遇到的所有人点头，无论你是否认识她们。

paragraphs.en: Matthew had taken the scrawny little hand awkwardly in his; then and there he decided what to do. He could not tell this child with the glowing eyes that there had been a mistake; he would take her home and let Marilla do that. She couldn’t be left at Bright River anyhow, no matter what mistake had been made, so all questions and explanations might as well be deferred until he was safely back at Green Gables. “I’m sorry I was late,” he said shyly. “Come along. The horse is over in the yard. Give me your bag.”
paragraphs.zh: 马修笨拙地握着那只骨瘦如柴的小手。当场他就决定要做什么。他无法告诉这个眼睛发光的孩子，这是一个错误；他会带她回家，让玛丽拉去做。无论如何，她不能被留在光明河，无论犯了什么错误，所以所有的问题和解释不妨推迟到他安全返回绿山墙为止。 “对不起，我迟到了。”他害羞地说。 “走吧。马在院子里。把你的包给我。”

paragraphs.en: “Well now, I’m afraid I can’t,” said Matthew, who was getting a little dizzy. He felt as he had once felt in his rash youth when another boy had enticed him on the merry-go-round at a picnic. “Well, whatever it was it must have been something nice because she was divinely beautiful. Have you ever imagined what it must feel like to be divinely beautiful?” “I have, often. Which would you rather be if you had the choice--divinely beautiful or dazzlingly clever or angelically good?” “Neither do I. I can never decide. But it doesn’t make much real difference for it isn’t likely I’ll ever be either. It’s certain I’ll never be angelically good. Mrs. Spencer says--oh, Mr. Cuthbert! Oh, Mr. Cuthbert!! Oh, Mr. Cuthbert!!!”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，恐怕我不能，”马修说，他有点头晕。他的感觉就像他年轻时鲁莽的时候，在野餐时另一个男孩引诱他坐旋转木马时的感觉一样。 “好吧，不管是什么，一定是件好事，因为她美丽非凡。你有没有想象过，美丽非凡是什么感觉？” “我经常这样。如果你有选择的话，你更愿意成为哪一个——神圣的美丽、耀眼的聪明还是天使般的善良？” “我也不知道。我永远无法决定。但这并没有多大真正的区别，因为我也不太可能成为那样的人。可以肯定的是，我永远不会成为天使般的好人。斯宾塞夫人说——哦，库斯伯特先生！哦，库斯伯特先生！！哦，库斯伯特先生！！！”

paragraphs.en: “Well now, yes. It always kind of gives me a thrill to see them ugly white grubs that spade up in the cucumber beds. I hate the look of them.” “Oh, I don’t think that can be exactly the same kind of a thrill. Do you think it can? There doesn’t seem to be much connection between grubs and lakes of shining waters, does there? But why do other people call it Barry’s pond?” “I reckon because Mr. Barry lives up there in that house. Orchard Slope’s the name of his place. If it wasn’t for that big bush behind it you could see Green Gables from here. But we have to go over the bridge and round by the road, so it’s near half a mile further.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，是的。看到那些丑陋的白色幼虫在黄瓜床上爬行，总是让我感到兴奋。我讨厌它们的样子。” “哦，我认为这不可能是完全相同的刺激。你认为可以吗？幼虫和波光粼粼的湖泊之间似乎没有太多联系，不是吗？但是为什么其他人称它为巴里池塘？” “我想是因为巴里先生就住在那栋房子里。果园坡是他家的名字。如果不是后面有大灌木丛，你从这里就能看到绿山墙。但我们必须过桥，绕着路走，所以又走了半英里。”

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Marilla Cuthbert is Surprised
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 3 章：玛丽拉·卡斯伯特的冷酷与震撼

paragraphs.en: MARILLA came briskly forward as Matthew opened the door. But when her eyes fell on the odd little figure in the stiff, ugly dress, with the long braids of red hair and the eager, luminous eyes, she stopped short in amazement. He nodded at the child, remembering that he had never even asked her name. “No boy! But there must have been a boy,” insisted Marilla. “We sent word to Mrs. Spencer to bring a boy.” “Well, she didn’t. She brought her. I asked the stationmaster. And I had to bring her home. She couldn’t be left there, no matter where the mistake had come in.”
paragraphs.zh: 马修打开门时，玛丽拉轻快地走上前。但当她的目光落在那个奇怪的小身影上时，她穿着僵硬丑陋的衣服，留着长长的红发辫子，眼睛热切而明亮，她惊讶地停了下来。他对孩子点点头，记得自己从来没有问过她的名字。 “没有男孩！但一定有一个男孩，”玛丽拉坚持说。 “我们通知斯宾塞夫人带一个男孩来。” “嗯，她没有。她把她带来了。我问了站长。我必须把她带回家。不管错误出在哪里，她都不能留在那里。”

paragraphs.en: “Unromantic fiddlesticks!” said the unsympathetic Marilla. “Anne is a real good plain sensible name. You’ve no need to be ashamed of it.” “Oh, I’m not ashamed of it,” explained Anne, “only I like Cordelia better. I’ve always imagined that my name was Cordelia--at least, I always have of late years. When I was young I used to imagine it was Geraldine, but I like Cordelia better now. But if you call me Anne please call me Anne spelled with an E.” “What difference does it make how it’s spelled?” asked Marilla with another rusty smile as she picked up the teapot.
paragraphs.zh: “不浪漫的小提琴！”毫无同情心的玛丽拉说道。 “安妮是一个真正美好、简单、明智的名字。你不必为此感到羞耻。” “哦，我并不为此感到羞耻，”安妮解释道，“只是我更喜欢科迪莉亚。我一直以为我的名字叫科迪莉亚——至少，最近几年我总是这么想。年轻的时候，我常常想象它是杰拉尔丁，但现在我更喜欢科迪莉亚了。但是如果你叫我安妮，请叫我拼写为 E 的安妮。” “它的拼写有什么区别？”玛丽拉拿起茶壶，脸上又带着生锈的微笑问道。

paragraphs.en: “I’ve never been in the depths of despair, so I can’t say,” responded Marilla. “Weren’t you? Well, did you ever try to imagine you were in the depths of despair?” “Then I don’t think you can understand what it’s like. It’s a very uncomfortable feeling indeed. When you try to eat a lump comes right up in your throat and you can’t swallow anything, not even if it was a chocolate caramel. I had one chocolate caramel once two years ago and it was simply delicious. I’ve often dreamed since then that I had a lot of chocolate caramels, but I always wake up just when I’m going to eat them. I do hope you won’t be offended because I can’t eat. Everything is extremely nice, but still I cannot eat.”
paragraphs.zh: “我从来没有陷入过绝望的深渊，所以我不能说，”玛丽拉回答道。 “不是吗？那么，你有没有尝试过想象自己正处于绝望的深渊？” “那我想你无法理解那是什么感觉。这确实是一种非常不舒服的感觉。当你试图吃东西时，喉咙里突然有一个肿块，你无法吞咽任何东西，即使它是巧克力焦糖。两年前我吃过一次巧克力焦糖，它真的很好吃。从那以后我经常梦见我有很多巧克力焦糖，但我总是在要吃它们的时候醒来。我真的希望你不会被冒犯了，因为我不能吃东西，一切都非常好，但我仍然不能吃东西。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, this is a pretty kettle of fish,” she said wrathfully. “This is what comes of sending word instead of going ourselves. Richard Spencer’s folks have twisted that message somehow. One of us will have to drive over and see Mrs. Spencer tomorrow, that’s certain. This girl will have to be sent back to the asylum.” “Well now, she’s a real nice little thing, Marilla. It’s kind of a pity to send her back when she’s so set on staying here.” “Matthew Cuthbert, you don’t mean to say you think we ought to keep her!” Marilla’s astonishment could not have been greater if Matthew had expressed a predilection for standing on his head.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，这真是一锅漂亮的鱼，”她愤怒地说。 “这就是发消息而不是亲自去的后果。理查德·斯宾塞的家人不知何故扭曲了这条信息。我们中的一个人明天必须开车过去见斯宾塞夫人，这是肯定的。这个女孩将不得不被送回精神病院。” “现在，她真是个可爱的小东西，玛丽拉。当她如此执意要留在这里时，把她送回去有点遗憾。” “马修·库斯伯特，你并不是说你认为我们应该保留她！”如果马修表示喜欢倒立的话，马里拉会更加惊讶。

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Morning at Green Gables
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 4 章：绿山墙的第一个清晨

paragraphs.en: IT was broad daylight when Anne awoke and sat up in bed, staring confusedly at the window through which a flood of cheery sunshine was pouring and outside of which something white and feathery waved across glimpses of blue sky. For a moment she could not remember where she was. First came a delightful thrill, as of something very pleasant; then a horrible remembrance. This was Green Gables and they didn’t want her because she wasn’t a boy!
paragraphs.zh: 安妮醒来时，已是大白天了，她从床上坐起来，困惑地盯着窗户，窗外洒满了明快的阳光，窗外有一些白色的、羽毛般的东西在蓝天上飘荡。一时间她记不起自己身在何处。首先是一种令人愉快的兴奋，就像是某种非常令人愉快的事情一样。然后是一个可怕的回忆。这是绿山墙，他们不想要她，因为她不是男孩！

paragraphs.en: Marilla really did not know how to talk to the child, and her uncomfortable ignorance made her crisp and curt when she did not mean to be. “Oh, isn’t it wonderful?” she said, waving her hand comprehensively at the good world outside. “It’s a big tree,” said Marilla, “and it blooms great, but the fruit don’t amount to much never--small and wormy.”
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉真的不知道如何和孩子说话，而她的无知让她在无意的时候变得干脆而生硬。 “噢，这不是很棒吗？”她一边说着，一边向外面的美好世界挥了挥手。 “这是一棵大树，”玛丽拉说，“花开得很好，但结的果子却并不多——又小又长虫。”

paragraphs.en: When the meal was ended Anne came out of her reverie and offered to wash the dishes. “Pretty well. I’m better at looking after children, though. I’ve had so much experience at that. It’s such a pity you haven’t any here for me to look after.” “I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man.” “I think he’s lovely,” said Anne reproachfully. “He is so very sympathetic. He didn’t mind how much I talked--he seemed to like it. I felt that he was a kindred spirit as soon as ever I saw him.”
paragraphs.zh: 吃完饭后，安妮从沉思中回过神来，主动提出要洗碗。 “很好。不过，我更擅长照顾孩子。这方面我有很多经验。可惜你这里没有孩子让我照顾。” “我觉得我不想再照顾比现在更多的孩子了。从良心来说，你已经够麻烦的了。我不知道该拿你怎么办。马修是个最可笑的人。” “我觉得他很可爱。”安妮责备地说。 “他非常富有同情心。他并不介意我说了多少——他似乎很喜欢。我一见到他就觉得他是志同道合的人。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I like things to have handles even if they are only geraniums. It makes them seem more like people. How do you know but that it hurts a geranium’s feelings just to be called a geranium and nothing else? You wouldn’t like to be called nothing but a woman all the time. Yes, I shall call it Bonny. I named that cherry-tree outside my bedroom window this morning. I called it Snow Queen because it was so white. Of course, it won’t always be in blossom, but one can imagine that it is, can’t one?”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我喜欢有把手的东西，即使它们只是天竺葵。这让它们看起来更像人。你怎么知道，仅仅被称为天竺葵而不是别的东西会伤害天竺葵的感情？你不会喜欢一直被称为女人。是的，我会叫它邦妮。今天早上我把卧室窗外的那棵樱桃树命名为“雪之女王”，因为它太白了。当然，它不会总是这样。盛开，但人们可以想象它是这样的，不是吗？”

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Anne's History
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 5 章：安妮坎坷凄凉的身世

paragraphs.en: DO you know,” said Anne confidentially, “I’ve made up my mind to enjoy this drive. It’s been my experience that you can nearly always enjoy things if you make up your mind firmly that you will. Of course, you must make it up firmly. I am not going to think about going back to the asylum while we’re having our drive. I’m just going to think about the drive. Oh, look, there’s one little early wild rose out! Isn’t it lovely? Don’t you think it must be glad to be a rose? Wouldn’t it be nice if roses could talk? I’m sure they could tell us such lovely things. And isn’t pink the most bewitching color in the world? I love it, but I can’t wear it. Redheaded people can’t wear pink, not even in imagination. Did you ever know of anybody whose hair was red when she was young, but got to be another color when she grew up?”
paragraphs.zh: 你知道吗，”安妮秘密地说，“我已经下定决心要享受这次驾车之旅。根据我的经验，如果你下定决心，你几乎总是可以享受事物。当然，一定要补足。当我们开车的时候，我不会考虑回到精神病院。我只想考虑一下驱动器。哦，看，一朵早开的野玫瑰已经长出来了！是不是很可爱？你不觉得成为一朵玫瑰一定很高兴吗？如果玫瑰会说话，那不是很好吗？我相信他们可以告诉我们如此可爱的事情。粉色难道不是世界上最迷人的颜色吗？我喜欢它，但我不能穿它。红头发的人不能穿粉色，即使在想象中也是如此。你知道有谁年轻时头发是红色的，但长大后却变成了另一种颜色吗？”

paragraphs.en: “It’s five miles; and as you’re evidently bent on talking you might as well talk to some purpose by telling me what you know about yourself.” “Oh, what I know about myself isn’t really worth telling,” said Anne eagerly. “If you’ll only let me tell you what I imagine about myself you’ll think it ever so much more interesting.” “No, I don’t want any of your imaginings. Just you stick to bald facts. Begin at the beginning. Where were you born and how old are you?”
paragraphs.zh: “有五英里；既然你显然一心想说话，那么你不妨通过告诉我你对自己的了解来达到某种目的。” “哦，我对自己的了解并不值得讲述。”安妮急切地说。 “如果你让我告诉你我对自己的想象，你会觉得这更有趣。” “不，我不需要你的任何想象。只要你坚持赤裸裸的事实。从头开始。你在哪里出生，多大了？”

paragraphs.en: “Mr. and Mrs. Thomas moved away from Bolingbroke to Marysville, and I lived with them until I was eight years old. I helped look after the Thomas children--there were four of them younger than me--and I can tell you they took a lot of looking after. Then Mr. Thomas was killed falling under a train and his mother offered to take Mrs. Thomas and the children, but she didn’t want me. Mrs. Thomas was at her wits’ end, so she said, what to do with me. Then Mrs. Hammond from up the river came down and said she’d take me, seeing I was handy with children, and I went up the river to live with her in a little clearing among the stumps. It was a very lonesome place. I’m sure I could never have lived there if I hadn’t had an imagination. Mr. Hammond worked a little sawmill up there, and Mrs. Hammond had eight children. She had twins three times. I like babies in moderation, but twins three times in succession is too much. I told Mrs. Hammond so firmly, when the last pair came. I used to get so dreadfully tired carrying them about.
paragraphs.zh: “托马斯先生和托马斯太太从博林布鲁克搬到了马里斯维尔，我和他们住在一起直到我八岁。我帮忙照顾托马斯的孩子们——其中有四个比我小——我可以告诉你，他们花了很多时间照顾。然后托马斯先生在火车下摔死了，他的母亲提出要带走托马斯太太和孩子们，但她不想要我。托马斯太太束手无策，所以她说，该怎么办？然后，河上游的哈蒙德太太过来，说她会带我去，我就到河上游去，住在树桩间的一块小空地里，我确信，如果哈蒙德先生在那里经营一家小锯木厂，我绝对不可能住在那里，而哈蒙德太太有八个孩子，但我喜欢双胞胎。当最后一双来的时候，我已经累得要命了。

paragraphs.en: Marilla asked no more questions. Anne gave herself up to a silent rapture over the shore road and Marilla guided the sorrel abstractedly while she pondered deeply. Pity was suddenly stirring in her heart for the child. What a starved, unloved life she had had--a life of drudgery and poverty and neglect; for Marilla was shrewd enough to read between the lines of Anne’s history and divine the truth. No wonder she had been so delighted at the prospect of a real home. It was a pity she had to be sent back. What if she, Marilla, should indulge Matthew’s unaccountable whim and let her stay? He was set on it; and the child seemed a nice, teachable little thing.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉没有再问什么。安妮默默地陶醉在海岸公路上，玛丽拉一边心不在焉地引导着栗色树，一边陷入沉思。她心中突然升起了对孩子的怜悯。她过着多么饥饿、不被爱的生活——苦差事、贫穷和被忽视的生活；因为玛丽拉足够精明，能够从安妮的历史字里行间看出真相。难怪她对拥有一个真正的家感到如此高兴。可惜她不得不被送回去。如果她，玛丽拉，应该纵容马修无法解释的突发奇想并让她留下来怎么办？他已经下定决心要这么做了。这孩子看上去是个可爱、好学的小东西。

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Marilla Makes Up Her Mind
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 6 章：玛丽拉下定决心收养

paragraphs.en: GET there they did, however, in due season. Mrs. Spencer lived in a big yellow house at White Sands Cove, and she came to the door with surprise and welcome mingled on her benevolent face. “Dear, dear,” she exclaimed, “you’re the last folks I was looking for today, but I’m real glad to see you. You’ll put your horse in? And how are you, Anne?” “I’m as well as can be expected, thank you,” said Anne smilelessly. A blight seemed to have descended on her.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，他们在适当的季节到达了那里。斯宾塞夫人住在白沙湾的一栋黄色大房子里，她来到门口时，慈祥的脸上夹杂着惊讶和欢迎。 “亲爱的，亲爱的，”她喊道，“你们是我今天最后找的人，但我真的很高兴见到你们。你会把你的马放进去吗？你好吗，安妮？” “我很好，谢谢你。”安妮微笑着说道。一场灾难似乎降临在她身上。

paragraphs.en: Marilla did not look as if she thought Providence had much to do with the matter. Here was an unexpectedly good chance to get this unwelcome orphan off her hands, and she did not even feel grateful for it. She knew Mrs. Peter Blewett only by sight as a small, shrewish-faced woman without an ounce of superfluous flesh on her bones. But she had heard of her. “A terrible worker and driver,” Mrs. Peter was said to be; and discharged servant girls told fearsome tales of her temper and stinginess, and her family of pert, quarrelsome children. Marilla felt a qualm of conscience at the thought of handing Anne over to her tender mercies.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉看起来似乎并不认为普罗维登斯与这件事有多大关系。这是一个意想不到的好机会，可以让这个不受欢迎的孤儿摆脱她的手，而她甚至没有对此感到感激。她只见过彼得·布卢伊特夫人，她身材娇小，面容泼辣，骨头上没有一丁点多余的肉。但她听说过她。据说彼得夫人是“一个糟糕的工人和司机”。被解雇的女仆讲述了她的脾气和吝啬的可怕故事，以及她的家庭中顽皮、爱吵架的孩子。一想到要把安妮交给她温柔的怜悯，马里拉就感到良心不安。

paragraphs.en: Marilla looked at Anne and softened at sight of the child’s pale face with its look of mute misery--the misery of a helpless little creature who finds itself once more caught in the trap from which it had escaped. Marilla felt an uncomfortable conviction that, if she denied the appeal of that look, it would haunt her to her dying day. Moreover, she did not fancy Mrs. Blewett. To hand a sensitive, “highstrung” child over to such a woman! No, she could not take the responsibility of doing that!
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉看着安妮，看到孩子苍白的脸和无言的痛苦表情，她的心软化了——这是一个无助的小动物发现自己再次陷入了它逃脱的陷阱的痛苦。玛丽拉感到一种不安的信念，如果她否认这种外表的吸引力，它会一直困扰着她直到她临死为止。而且，她也不喜欢布卢伊特夫人。把一个敏感、“神经质”的孩子交给这样一个女人！不，她不能承担那样的责任！

paragraphs.en: When they arrived back at Green Gables that evening Matthew met them in the lane. Marilla from afar had noted him prowling along it and guessed his motive. She was prepared for the relief she read in his face when he saw that she had at least brought Anne back with her. But she said nothing, to him, relative to the affair, until they were both out in the yard behind the barn milking the cows. Then she briefly told him Anne’s history and the result of the interview with Mrs. Spencer. “I wouldn’t give a dog I liked to that Blewett woman,” said Matthew with unusual vim.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，当他们回到绿山墙时，马修在小巷里遇见了他们。玛丽拉远远地注意到他沿着这条路徘徊，并猜出了他的动机。当他看到她至少把安妮带回来时，她从他脸上看到的轻松感已经做好了准备。但她没有对他提及这件事，直到他们俩都到谷仓后面的院子里挤牛奶。然后她简单地向他讲述了安妮的历史以及斯宾塞夫人的采访结果。 “我不会把我喜欢的狗送给那个布勒伊特女人，”马修异常生气地说。

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Anne Says Her Prayers
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 7 章：安妮的第一次奇特祷告

paragraphs.en: WHEN Marilla took Anne up to bed that night she said stiffly: “Now, Anne, I noticed last night that you threw your clothes all about the floor when you took them off. That is a very untidy habit, and I can’t allow it at all. As soon as you take off any article of clothing fold it neatly and place it on the chair. I haven’t any use at all for little girls who aren’t neat.” “I was so harrowed up in my mind last night that I didn’t think about my clothes at all,” said Anne. “I’ll fold them nicely tonight. They always made us do that at the asylum. Half the time, though, I’d forget, I’d be in such a hurry to get into bed nice and quiet and imagine things.”
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，玛丽拉把安妮抱上床，生硬地说：“安妮，我昨晚注意到你脱衣服的时候把衣服扔得满地都是。这是一个非常不整洁的习惯，我根本不允许这样做。你一脱下任何衣服，就把它折叠整齐，放在椅子上。不整洁的小女孩对我来说根本没有任何用处。” “昨晚我心里非常难过，根本没有想到我的衣服，”安妮说。 “今晚我会把它们叠好。在精神病院时他们总是让我们这样做。不过，有一半的时间我会忘记，我会匆忙地安静地躺在床上，想象一些事情。”

paragraphs.en: “So you do know something then, thank goodness! You’re not quite a heathen. Where did you learn that?” “Oh, at the asylum Sunday-school. They made us learn the whole catechism. I liked it pretty well. There’s something splendid about some of the words. ‘Infinite, eternal and unchangeable.’ Isn’t that grand? It has such a roll to it--just like a big organ playing. You couldn’t quite call it poetry, I suppose, but it sounds a lot like it, doesn’t it?” “We’re not talking about poetry, Anne--we are talking about saying your prayers. Don’t you know it’s a terrible wicked thing not to say your prayers every night? I’m afraid you are a very bad little girl.”
paragraphs.zh: “所以你确实知道一些事情，谢天谢地！你不完全是异教徒。你从哪里学到的？” “哦，在精神病院的主日学校。他们让我们学习整个教义问答。我很喜欢它。其中一些词很精彩。‘无限、永恒和不变。’这不是很伟大吗？它有这样的滚动——就像一个大风琴演奏一样。我想你不能完全称它为诗，但听起来很像，不是吗？” “我们不是在谈论诗歌，安妮——我们是在谈论祈祷。你难道不知道每天晚上不祈祷是一件可怕的邪恶的事情吗？我担心你是一个非常坏的小女孩。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, of course, if you want me to,” assented Anne cheerfully. “I’d do anything to oblige you. But you’ll have to tell me what to say for this once. After I get into bed I’ll imagine out a real nice prayer to say always. I believe that it will be quite interesting, now that I come to think of it.” “Why must people kneel down to pray? If I really wanted to pray I’ll tell you what I’d do. I’d go out into a great big field all alone or into the deep, deep woods, and I’d look up into the sky--up--up--up--into that lovely blue sky that looks as if there was no end to its blueness. And then I’d just feel a prayer. Well, I’m ready. What am I to say?”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，如果你愿意的话，”安妮高兴地表示同意。 “我愿意做任何事情来满足你。但是你必须告诉我这一次要说什么。我上床睡觉后，我会想象出一个真正美好的祈祷，永远要说。我相信，现在我想起来了，这会很有趣。” “为什么人们必须跪下来祈祷？如果我真的想祈祷，我会告诉你我会做什么。我会独自走到一大片大田里，或者走进很深很深的树林，然后我会抬头仰望天空——向上——向上——向上——那可爱的蓝天，看起来好像没有尽头的蓝色。然后我就会感受到一种祈祷。好吧，我准备好了。我该说什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: Poor Marilla was only preserved from complete collapse by remembering that it was not irreverence, but simply spiritual ignorance on the part of Anne that was responsible for this extraordinary petition. She tucked the child up in bed, mentally vowing that she should be taught a prayer the very next day, and was leaving the room with the light when Anne called her back. “I’ve just thought of it now. I should have said ‘Amen’ in place of ‘yours respectfully,’ shouldn’t I?--the way the ministers do. I’d forgotten it, but I felt a prayer should be finished off in some way, so I put in the other. Do you suppose it will make any difference?”
paragraphs.zh: 可怜的玛丽拉只有记住，安妮造成这一非同寻常的请愿并不是不敬，而是精神上的无知，才免于彻底崩溃。她把孩子盖在床上，心里发誓第二天就应该教她祈祷，当安妮叫她回来时，她正准备离开开着灯的房间。 “我现在才想起来。我应该说‘阿门’来代替‘恭敬的’，不是吗？就像牧师们做的那样。我忘了，但我觉得祈祷应该以某种方式结束，所以我加上了另一个。你认为这会有什么不同吗？”

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Anne's Bringing-up is Begun
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 8 章：绿山墙的养育生活开启

paragraphs.en: FOR reasons best known to herself, Marilla did not tell Anne that she was to stay at Green Gables until the next afternoon. During the forenoon she kept the child busy with various tasks and watched over her with a keen eye while she did them. By noon she had concluded that Anne was smart and obedient, willing to work and quick to learn; her most serious shortcoming seemed to be a tendency to fall into daydreams in the middle of a task and forget all about it until such time as she was sharply recalled to earth by a reprimand or a catastrophe.
paragraphs.zh: 由于她自己最清楚的原因，玛丽拉没有告诉安妮她要在绿山墙呆到第二天下午。整个上午，她让孩子忙着做各种事情，并在她做这些事情时用敏锐的目光注视着她。到了中午，她得出结论，安妮聪明、听话、愿意工作、学得很快。她最严重的缺点似乎是在工作中容易陷入白日梦，然后忘记一切，直到受到斥责或灾难才将她拉回现实。

paragraphs.en: “Do you never imagine things different from what they really are?” asked Anne wide-eyed. “Oh!” Anne drew a long breath. “Oh, Miss--Marilla, how much you miss!” “I don’t believe in imagining things different from what they really are,” retorted Marilla. “When the Lord puts us in certain circumstances He doesn’t mean for us to imagine them away. And that reminds me. Go into the sitting room, Anne--be sure your feet are clean and don’t let any flies in--and bring me out the illustrated card that’s on the mantelpiece. The Lord’s Prayer is on it and you’ll devote your spare time this afternoon to learning it off by heart. There’s to be no more of such praying as I heard last night.”
paragraphs.zh: “你从来没有想象过与实际情况不同的事情吗？”安妮睁大眼睛问道。 “哦！”安妮长长地吸了一口气。 “哦，玛丽拉小姐，你多么想念啊！” “我不相信想象的事情与实际情况不同，”玛丽拉反驳道。 “当主把我们置于某些环境中时，他并不是要我们想象它们会消失。这提醒了我。安妮，到客厅去——确保你的脚干净，不要让苍蝇进来——然后把壁炉架上的带插图的卡片拿出来给我。上面有主祷文，你今天下午要用空闲时间背诵它。不要再像我昨晚听到的那样祈祷了。”

paragraphs.en: “Marilla,” she demanded presently, “do you think that I shall ever have a bosom friend in Avonlea?” “A bosom friend--an intimate friend, you know--a really kindred spirit to whom I can confide my inmost soul. I’ve dreamed of meeting her all my life. I never really supposed I would, but so many of my loveliest dreams have come true all at once that perhaps this one will, too. Do you think it’s possible?”
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉，”她立刻问道，“你认为我在埃文利会有一个知音吗？” “一位知己——一位亲密的朋友，你知道——一位真正志同道合的人，我可以向她倾诉我内心深处的情感。我一生都梦想着见到她。我从来没有真正想过我会这么做，但我的许多最可爱的梦想一下子都实现了，也许这个也能实现。你认为这可能吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I know it pretty nearly all now--all but just the last line.” “Well, never mind, do as I tell you. Go to your room and finish learning it well, and stay there until I call you down to help me get tea.” “Can I take the apple blossoms with me for company?” pleaded Anne. “No; you don’t want your room cluttered up with flowers. You should have left them on the tree in the first place.” “I did feel a little that way, too,” said Anne. “I kind of felt I shouldn’t shorten their lovely lives by picking them--I wouldn’t want to be picked if I were an apple blossom. But the temptation was irresistible. What do you do when you meet with an irresistible temptation?”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我现在几乎都知道了——除了最后一行。” “好吧，没关系，按我说的做，去你的房间好好学完，待在那里直到我叫你下去帮我倒茶。” “我可以带着苹果花作伴吗？”安妮恳求道。 “不；你不想让你的房间堆满鲜花。你一开始就应该把它们留在树上。” “我确实也有一点这样的感觉，”安妮说。 “我有点觉得我不应该因为采摘而缩短它们可爱的生命——如果我是一朵苹果花，我也不想被采摘。但诱惑是不可抗拒的。当你遇到不可抗拒的诱惑时，你会怎么做？”

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is Properly Terrified
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 9 章：林德太太的批评与安妮发火

paragraphs.en: ANNE had been a fortnight at Green Gables before Mrs. Lynde arrived to inspect her. Mrs. Rachel, to do her justice, was not to blame for this. A severe and unseasonable attack of grippe had confined that good lady to her house ever since the occasion of her last visit to Green Gables. Mrs. Rachel was not often sick and had a well-defined contempt for people who were; but grippe, she asserted, was like no other illness on earth and could only be interpreted as one of the special visitations of Providence. As soon as her doctor allowed her to put her foot out-of-doors she hurried up to Green Gables, bursting with curiosity to see Matthew and Marilla’s orphan, concerning whom all sorts of stories and suppositions had gone abroad in Avonlea.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在林德夫人来视察之前已经在绿山墙呆了两周了。公平地说，雷切尔夫人不应为此承担责任。自从上次访问绿山墙以来，一场严重的、不合时宜的流行性感冒发作，让这位好心的女士一直待在家里。雷切尔夫人并不经常生病，而且对生病的人怀有明显的蔑视。但她断言，流行性感冒与地球上任何其他疾病都不一样，只能被解释为上帝的特殊降临之一。医生一允许她出门，她就急忙赶到绿山墙，满怀好奇地想看看马修和玛丽拉的孤儿，关于他的各种故事和猜测已经在埃文利流传开来。

paragraphs.en: “I’m not feeling discouraged,” was Marilla’s dry response, “when I make up my mind to do a thing it stays made up. I suppose you’d like to see Anne. I’ll call her in.” Anne came running in presently, her face sparkling with the delight of her orchard rovings; but, abashed at finding the delight herself in the unexpected presence of a stranger, she halted confusedly inside the door. She certainly was an odd-looking little creature in the short tight wincey dress she had worn from the asylum, below which her thin legs seemed ungracefully long. Her freckles were more numerous and obtrusive than ever; the wind had ruffled her hatless hair into over-brilliant disorder; it had never looked redder than at that moment.
paragraphs.zh: “我并没有感到灰心丧气，”玛丽拉干巴巴地回答，“当我下定决心要做一件事时，它就一直是下定决心的。我想你想见安妮。我会叫她进来的。”不久，安妮跑了进来，她的脸因果园漫游的喜悦而闪闪发光。但是，她为自己在陌生人的意外出现中找到乐趣而感到羞愧，困惑地在门内停了下来。穿着从疯人院出来时穿的紧身短裙，她确实是个看上去很奇怪的小东西，裙子下面她的细腿显得长得不雅观。她的雀斑比以往任何时候都更多、更引人注目。风把她没戴帽子的头发吹得乱七八糟。它从来没有比那一刻更红过。

paragraphs.en: Marilla opened her lips to say she knew not what of apology or deprecation. What she did say was a surprise to herself then and ever afterwards. “Marilla Cuthbert, you don’t mean to say that you are upholding her in such a terrible display of temper as we’ve just seen?” demanded Mrs. Rachel indignantly. “No,” said Marilla slowly, “I’m not trying to excuse her. She’s been very naughty and I’ll have to give her a talking to about it. But we must make allowances for her. She’s never been taught what is right. And you were too hard on her, Rachel.” Marilla could not help tacking on that last sentence, although she was again surprised at herself for doing it. Mrs. Rachel got up with an air of offended dignity.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉张开双唇，表示她不知道该道歉还是不赞成。她所说的话让当时和以后的自己都感到惊讶。 “玛丽拉·库斯伯特，你的意思不是说你在支持她，就像我们刚才看到的那样，表现出如此可怕的脾气？”雷切尔夫人愤怒地问道。 “不，”玛丽拉慢慢地说，“我不是想原谅她。她太调皮了，我得跟她谈谈。但我们必须体谅她。她从来没有被教导过什么是正确的。而且你对她太严厉了，雷切尔。”玛丽拉忍不住补充了最后一句话，尽管她再次对自己这么做感到惊讶。雷切尔夫人站起身来，脸上带着一种被冒犯的尊严。

paragraphs.en: “You hadn’t any right to fly into such a fury and talk the way you did to her, Anne. I was ashamed of you--thoroughly ashamed of you. I wanted you to behave nicely to Mrs. Lynde, and instead of that you have disgraced me. I’m sure I don’t know why you should lose your temper like that just because Mrs. Lynde said you were red-haired and homely. You say it yourself often enough.”
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你没有权利大发雷霆，用你对她的方式说话。我为你感到羞耻——彻底为你感到羞耻。我希望你对林德太太表现得友善，但你却让我丢脸。我确信我不知道你为什么要这样发脾气，仅仅因为林德太太说你是红发的，相貌平平。你自己也经常这么说。”

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Anne's Apology
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 10 章：安妮戏剧化的道歉

paragraphs.en: MARILLA said nothing to Matthew about the affair that evening; but when Anne proved still refractory the next morning an explanation had to be made to account for her absence from the breakfast table. Marilla told Matthew the whole story, taking pains to impress him with a due sense of the enormity of Anne’s behavior. “It’s a good thing Rachel Lynde got a calling down; she’s a meddlesome old gossip,” was Matthew’s consolatory rejoinder. “Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you. You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!”
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，玛丽拉没有向马修提及这件事。但第二天早上，当安妮仍然难以控制时，必须对她缺席早餐桌做出解释。玛丽拉向马修讲述了整个故事，并煞费苦心地让他对安妮行为的严重性产生应有的认识。 “雷切尔·林德接到电话是一件好事；她是个爱管闲事的老八卦者，”马修安慰性地反驳道。 “马修·库斯伯特，我对你感到惊讶。你知道安妮的行为很可怕，但你却支持她！我想你接下来会说她根本不应该受到惩罚！”

paragraphs.en: Matthew recollected that he must say what he had come to say without loss of time, lest Marilla return prematurely. “Well now, Anne, don’t you think you’d better do it and have it over with?” he whispered. “It’ll have to be done sooner or later, you know, for Marilla’s a dreadful determined woman--dreadful determined, Anne. Do it right off, I say, and have it over.” “Yes--apologize--that’s the very word,” said Matthew eagerly. “Just smooth it over so to speak. That’s what I was trying to get at.”
paragraphs.zh: 马修想起来，他必须抓紧时间说完自己要说的话，免得玛丽拉过早回来。 “好吧，安妮，你不认为你最好还是把这件事结束吧？”他低声说道。 “这件事迟早要完成，你知道，因为玛丽拉是个意志坚定得可怕的女人——意志坚定得可怕，安妮。我说，马上就做，然后就结束了。” “是的——道歉——就是这个词，”马修急切地说。 “可以这么说，只是让它变得平滑。这就是我想要达到的目的。”

paragraphs.en: This was satisfactory--or should have been so. But Marilla could not rid herself of the notion that something in her scheme of punishment was going askew. Anne had no business to look so rapt and radiant. Rapt and radiant Anne continued until they were in the very presence of Mrs. Lynde, who was sitting knitting by her kitchen window. Then the radiance vanished. Mournful penitence appeared on every feature. Before a word was spoken Anne suddenly went down on her knees before the astonished Mrs. Rachel and held out her hands beseechingly.
paragraphs.zh: 这是令人满意的——或者说应该如此。但玛丽拉无法摆脱这样的想法：她的惩罚计划中有些东西出了问题。安妮没必要显得如此全神贯注、容光焕发。安妮全神贯注、容光焕发地继续说着，直到林德太太出现在他们面前，林德太太正坐在厨房的窗边织毛衣。然后光芒消失了。每一个面容上都流露出悲痛的悔罪之情。还没等说话，安妮突然跪倒在惊讶的雷切尔夫人面前，恳求地伸出双手。

paragraphs.en: “You did it thoroughly, all right enough,” was Marilla’s comment. Marilla was dismayed at finding herself inclined to laugh over the recollection. She had also an uneasy feeling that she ought to scold Anne for apologizing so well; but then, that was ridiculous! She compromised with her conscience by saying severely: “I hope you won’t have occasion to make many more such apologies. I hope you’ll try to control your temper now, Anne.” “That wouldn’t be so hard if people wouldn’t twit me about my looks,” said Anne with a sigh. “I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?”
paragraphs.zh: “你做得很彻底，很好，”玛丽拉评论道。玛丽拉沮丧地发现自己很容易因为回忆而发笑。她还有一种不安的感觉，她应该责骂安妮道歉得这么好。但那时，这太荒谬了！她良心妥协，严肃道：“希望你以后不要再有这样的道歉了。希望你现在能控制住自己的脾气，安妮。” “如果人们不因为我的外表而取笑我，那就不那么难了，”安妮叹了口气说。 “我不会对其他事情生气；但我厌倦了别人对我头发的嘲笑，这让我很生气。你认为我长大后的头发真的会变成漂亮的赤褐色吗？”

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Anne's Impressions of Sunday School
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 11 章：主日学的戴花帽子风波

paragraphs.en: Anne was standing in the gable room, looking solemnly at three new dresses spread out on the bed. One was of snuffy colored gingham which Marilla had been tempted to buy from a peddler the preceding summer because it looked so serviceable; one was of black-and-white checkered sateen which she had picked up at a bargain counter in the winter; and one was a stiff print of an ugly blue shade which she had purchased that week at a Carmody store. She had made them up herself, and they were all made alike--plain skirts fulled tightly to plain waists, with sleeves as plain as waist and skirt and tight as sleeves could be.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮站在山墙房里，表情严肃地看着床上铺着的三件新衣服。其中一件是颜色鲜艳的格子布，去年夏天，玛丽拉很想从小贩那里买下来，因为它看起来很实用。一件是黑白格子棉缎，是她冬天在特价柜台买的；一件是她冬天在特价柜台买的。其中一张是一张丑陋的蓝色图案的硬板印刷品，是她那周在卡莫迪商店购买的。都是她自己缝制的，而且都是一样的——朴素的裙子，紧紧地塞到朴素的腰部，袖子和腰身、裙子一样朴素，袖子尽可能地紧。

paragraphs.en: “But I’d rather look ridiculous when everybody else does than plain and sensible all by myself,” persisted Anne mournfully. “Trust you for that! Well, hang those dresses carefully up in your closet, and then sit down and learn the Sunday-school lesson. I got a quarterly from Mr. Bell for you and you’ll go to Sunday-school tomorrow,” said Marilla, disappearing downstairs in high dudgeon. “I did hope there would be a white one with puffed sleeves,” she whispered disconsolately. “I prayed for one, but I didn’t much expect it on that account. I didn’t suppose God would have time to bother about a little orphan girl’s dress. I knew I’d just have to depend on Marilla for it. Well, fortunately I can imagine that one of them is of snow-white muslin with lovely lace frills and three-puffed sleeves.”
paragraphs.zh: “但我宁愿在其他人都这样做的时候显得可笑，也不愿自己一个人显得朴素而明智，”安妮悲伤地坚持道。 “相信你！好吧，把那些衣服小心地挂在你的衣柜里，然后坐下来学习主日学校的课程。我从贝尔先生那里给你买了一本季刊，你明天就可以去主日学校了。”玛丽拉说着，气愤地走下楼去。 “我确实希望有一件白色的，泡泡袖的，”她沮丧地低声说道。 “我祈求能得到一件，但我并没有抱太大的希望。我以为上帝不会有时间去关心一个小孤女的衣服。我知道我只能依靠玛丽拉来穿。好吧，幸运的是，我可以想象其中一件是雪白的平纹细布制成的，上面有可爱的蕾丝褶边和三泡泡袖。”

paragraphs.en: When she had reached Mrs. Lynde’s house she found that lady gone. Nothing daunted, Anne proceeded onward to the church alone. In the porch she found a crowd of little girls, all more or less gaily attired in whites and blues and pinks, and all staring with curious eyes at this stranger in their midst, with her extraordinary head adornment. Avonlea little girls had already heard queer stories about Anne. Mrs. Lynde said she had an awful temper; Jerry Buote, the hired boy at Green Gables, said she talked all the time to herself or to the trees and flowers like a crazy girl. They looked at her and whispered to each other behind their quarterlies. Nobody made any friendly advances, then or later on when the opening exercises were over and Anne found herself in Miss Rogerson’s class.
paragraphs.zh: 当她到达林德太太家时，她发现那位女士已经不见了。安妮毫不畏惧，独自前往教堂。她在门廊里发现了一群小女孩，她们或多或少都穿着白色、蓝色和粉色的衣服，都用好奇的眼睛盯着她们中间这个戴着非凡头饰的陌生人。埃文利的小女孩们已经听说过有关安妮的奇怪故事。林德太太说她脾气很坏。杰瑞·博特（Jerry Buote）是绿山墙公园的雇工，他说她总是像个疯狂的女孩一样自言自语，或者对着树木和花朵说话。他们看着她，在季刊后面窃窃私语。无论是当时还是后来，当开场练习结束后，安妮发现自己在罗杰森小姐的课堂上时，都没有人做出任何友好的举动。

paragraphs.en: “But he wasn’t talking to me,” protested Anne. “He was talking to God and he didn’t seem to be very much interested in it, either. I think he thought God was too far off though. There was a long row of white birches hanging over the lake and the sunshine fell down through them, ‘way, ‘way down, deep into the water. Oh, Marilla, it was like a beautiful dream! It gave me a thrill and I just said, ‘Thank you for it, God,’ two or three times.”
paragraphs.zh: “但他没有跟我说话，”安妮抗议道。 “他在和上帝说话，而且他似乎对此也不太感兴趣。不过我想他认为上帝离得太远了。湖上悬挂着一长排白桦树，阳光透过它们洒下来，‘一路，‘一路向下，深入水里。哦，玛丽拉，这就像一个美丽的梦！这让我兴奋不已，我只说了两三遍‘谢谢你，上帝’。”

chapters.title: Chapter 12: A Solemn Vow and Promise
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 12 章：与戴安娜结为知心誓友

paragraphs.en: IT was not until the next Friday that Marilla heard the story of the flower-wreathed hat. She came home from Mrs. Lynde’s and called Anne to account. “Anne, Mrs. Rachel says you went to church last Sunday with your hat rigged out ridiculous with roses and buttercups. What on earth put you up to such a caper? A pretty-looking object you must have been!” “Oh. I know pink and yellow aren’t becoming to me,” began Anne. “Becoming fiddlesticks! It was putting flowers on your hat at all, no matter what color they were, that was ridiculous. You are the most aggravating child!” “I don’t see why it’s any more ridiculous to wear flowers on your hat than on your dress,” protested Anne. “Lots of little girls there had bouquets pinned on their dresses. What’s the difference?”
paragraphs.zh: 直到下周五，玛丽拉才听到了花环帽子的故事。她从林德太太家回到家，要求安妮负责。 “安妮，雷切尔太太说你上周日去了教堂，帽子上装饰着玫瑰和毛茛花，可笑了。到底是什么让你做出这样的举动？你一定是个漂亮的东西！” “哦。我知道粉色和黄色不适合我，”安妮开始说道。 “变成拉小提琴的人了！简直就是在帽子上插花，不管花什么颜色，太可笑了。你才是最可气的孩子！” “我不明白为什么在帽子上戴花比在衣服上戴花更可笑，”安妮抗议道。 “那里很多小女孩的衣服上都别着花束。有什么区别吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened--now that it has come I’m actually frightened. What if she shouldn’t like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life.” “Now, don’t get into a fluster. And I do wish you wouldn’t use such long words. It sounds so funny in a little girl. I guess Diana ‘ll like you well enough. It’s her mother you’ve got to reckon with. If she doesn’t like you it won’t matter how much Diana does. If she has heard about your outburst to Mrs. Lynde and going to church with buttercups round your hat I don’t know what she’ll think of you. You must be polite and well behaved, and don’t make any of your startling speeches. For pity’s sake, if the child isn’t actually trembling!”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，玛丽拉，我很害怕——现在它来了，我真的很害怕。如果她不喜欢我怎么办！这将是我一生中最悲惨的失望。” “现在，别慌了。我真希望你不要用这么长的词。这对一个小女孩来说听起来很有趣。我想戴安娜会很喜欢你的。你必须考虑的是她的母亲。如果她不喜欢你，戴安娜有多喜欢也没关系。如果她听说你对林德夫人发脾气，并在帽子上戴着毛茛去教堂，我不知道她会怎么想你。你必须有礼貌，表现得好，如果孩子没有真正颤抖的话，不要发表任何令人震惊的言论。”

paragraphs.en: “This is my little girl Diana,” said Mrs. Barry. “Diana, you might take Anne out into the garden and show her your flowers. It will be better for you than straining your eyes over that book. She reads entirely too much--” this to Marilla as the little girls went out--“and I can’t prevent her, for her father aids and abets her. She’s always poring over a book. I’m glad she has the prospect of a playmate--perhaps it will take her more out-of-doors.” Outside in the garden, which was full of mellow sunset light streaming through the dark old firs to the west of it, stood Anne and Diana, gazing bashfully at each other over a clump of gorgeous tiger lilies.
paragraphs.zh: “这是我的小女儿戴安娜，”巴里夫人说。 “戴安娜，你可以带安妮去花园，给她看你的花。这对你来说比盯着那本书更好。她读得太多了——”小女孩们出去时，这是对玛丽拉说的——“我无法阻止她，因为她父亲帮助和怂恿她。她总是埋头读书。我很高兴她有一个玩伴——也许这会让她更多地户外活动。”外面的花园里，柔和的夕阳透过西边深色的老冷杉洒下来，安妮和戴安娜站在花园里，在一丛华丽的虎百合面前羞涩地凝视着对方。

paragraphs.en: “You’re a queer girl, Anne. I heard before that you were queer. But I believe I’m going to like you real well.” When Marilla and Anne went home Diana went with them as far as the log bridge. The two little girls walked with their arms about each other. At the brook they parted with many promises to spend the next afternoon together. “Well, did you find Diana a kindred spirit?” asked Marilla as they went up through the garden of Green Gables.
paragraphs.zh: “你是个酷儿女孩，安妮。我以前听说你是个酷儿。但我相信我会非常喜欢你。”当玛丽拉和安妮回家时，戴安娜和他们一起一直走到独木桥。两个小女孩互相搂着对方走路。在小溪边，他们告别时许下许多诺言，要一起度过第二天下午。 “嗯，你觉得戴安娜志趣相投吗？”当他们穿过绿山墙花园时，玛丽拉问道。

chapters.title: Chapter 13: The Delights of Anticipation
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 13 章：期待主日学野餐的喜悦

paragraphs.en: IT’S time Anne was in to do her sewing,” said Marilla, glancing at the clock and then out into the yellow August afternoon where everything drowsed in the heat. “She stayed playing with Diana more than half an hour more ‘n I gave her leave to; and now she’s perched out there on the woodpile talking to Matthew, nineteen to the dozen, when she knows perfectly well she ought to be at her work. And of course he’s listening to her like a perfect ninny. I never saw such an infatuated man. The more she talks and the odder the things she says, the more he’s delighted evidently. Anne Shirley, you come right in here this minute, do you hear me!”
paragraphs.zh: 安妮该进去做针线活了，”玛丽拉看了一眼时钟，然后走进了八月的黄色午后，一切都在炎热中昏昏欲睡。“在我允许她玩之前，她又和戴安娜玩了半个多小时。现在她正坐在柴堆上和马修说话，一打十九，而她非常清楚自己应该去工作。当然，他像个完美的傻瓜一样听着她说话。我从未见过如此痴情的男人。她说得越多，说的话越奇怪，他显然就越高兴。安妮·雪莉，你现在就过来，听到了吗！”

paragraphs.en: “Why, I meant to, Marilla, as much as could be. But you have no idea how fascinating Idlewild is. And then, of course, I had to tell Matthew about the picnic. Matthew is such a sympathetic listener. Please can I go?” “You’ll have to learn to resist the fascination of Idle-whatever-you-call-it. When I tell you to come in at a certain time I mean that time and not half an hour later. And you needn’t stop to discourse with sympathetic listeners on your way, either. As for the picnic, of course you can go. You’re a Sunday-school scholar, and it’s not likely I’d refuse to let you go when all the other little girls are going.”
paragraphs.zh: “为什么，玛丽拉，我本想尽可能多的。但是你不知道艾德怀尔德有多么迷人。然后，当然，我必须告诉马修关于野餐的事情。马修是一位很有同情心的倾听者。我可以去吗？” “你得学会抵制‘无所事事’的魅力。当我告诉你在某个时间进来时，我指的是那个时间，而不是半小时后。而且你也不必在路上停下来与同情的听众交谈。至于野餐，你当然可以去。你是主日学的学生，当其他小女孩都走了时，我不可能拒绝让你走。”

paragraphs.en: “There, there, never mind your kissing nonsense. I’d sooner see you doing strictly as you’re told. As for cooking, I mean to begin giving you lessons in that some of these days. But you’re so featherbrained, Anne, I’ve been waiting to see if you’d sober down a little and learn to be steady before I begin. You’ve got to keep your wits about you in cooking and not stop in the middle of things to let your thoughts rove all over creation. Now, get out your patchwork and have your square done before teatime.”
paragraphs.zh: “好了，好了，别介意你那些胡言乱语的接吻。我宁愿看到你严格按照吩咐去做。至于烹饪，我打算这几天开始给你上这方面的课。但是你太轻率了，安妮，我一直在等着看你是否能清醒一点，学会在我开始之前保持稳定。你在烹饪中必须保持头脑清醒，不要半途而废，让你的思想在创造物中徘徊。现在，拿出你的拼布作品，在下午茶时间之前把你的正方形完成。”

paragraphs.en: “Such a thrill as went up and down my back, Marilla! I don’t think I’d ever really believed until then that there was honestly going to be a picnic. I couldn’t help fearing I’d only imagined it. But when a minister says a thing in the pulpit you just have to believe it.” “You set your heart too much on things, Anne,” said Marilla, with a sigh. “I’m afraid there’ll be a great many disappointments in store for you through life.”
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉，我的后背感到无比的激动！直到那时我才真正相信会有一场野餐。我不禁担心自己只是想象出来的。但是当牧师在讲坛上说某件事时，你就必须相信它。” “安妮，你太用心了，”玛丽拉叹了口气说。 “我担心你一生中将会有很多失望。”

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Anne's Confession
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 14 章：紫水晶胸针误会与假坦白

paragraphs.en: ON the Monday evening before the picnic Marilla came down from her room with a troubled face. “Anne,” she said to that small personage, who was shelling peas by the spotless table and singing, “Nelly of the Hazel Dell” with a vigor and expression that did credit to Diana’s teaching, “did you see anything of my amethyst brooch? I thought I stuck it in my pincushion when I came home from church yesterday evening, but I can’t find it anywhere.” “I--I saw it this afternoon when you were away at the Aid Society,” said Anne, a little slowly. “I was passing your door when I saw it on the cushion, so I went in to look at it.”
paragraphs.zh: 周一晚上，野餐前，玛丽拉从房间里走出来，一脸的困惑。 “安妮，”她对那个在一尘不染的桌子旁剥豌豆、唱着《榛树谷的耐莉》的小人物说，“你看到我的紫水晶胸针了吗？昨天晚上我从教堂回家时，我以为我把它插在了针垫里，但我到处都找不到它。” “我——今天下午你去援助协会的时候我看到了，”安妮语气有点慢。 “我路过你家门口的时候，看到垫子上有这个东西，所以就进去看了看。”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know what I wouldn’t sooner have had happen,” thought Marilla, as she nervously shelled the peas. “Of course, I don’t suppose she meant to steal it or anything like that. She’s just taken it to play with or help along that imagination of hers. She must have taken it, that’s clear, for there hasn’t been a soul in that room since she was in it, by her own story, until I went up tonight. And the brooch is gone, there’s nothing surer. I suppose she has lost it and is afraid to own up for fear she’ll be punished. It’s a dreadful thing to think she tells falsehoods. It’s a far worse thing than her fit of temper. It’s a fearful responsibility to have a child in your house you can’t trust. Slyness and untruthfulness--that’s what she has displayed. I declare I feel worse about that than about the brooch. If she’d only have told the truth about it I wouldn’t mind so much.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道如果不早点发生什么，”马里拉一边紧张地剥豌豆壳一边想。 “当然，我不认为她打算偷它或类似的东西。她只是拿它来玩弄或帮助她的想象力。很明显，她肯定拿走了它，因为根据她自己的说法，自从她在那个房间里以来，直到我今晚上去之前，那个房间里就没有一个灵魂。胸针不见了，没有什么比这更确定的了。我想她已经把它弄丢了，并且不敢承认，因为担心会受到惩罚。这是一个认为她说谎是一件比她的脾气更糟糕的事情，这是一种可怕的责任，她的狡猾和不诚实——这就是她所表现出的，如果她只说实话，我不会那么介意。

paragraphs.en: Marilla felt hot anger surge up into her heart again. This child had taken and lost her treasured amethyst brooch and now sat there calmly reciting the details thereof without the least apparent compunction or repentance. “Anne, this is terrible,” she said, trying to speak calmly. “You are the very wickedest girl I ever heard of.” “Yes, I suppose I am,” agreed Anne tranquilly. “And I know I’ll have to be punished. It’ll be your duty to punish me, Marilla. Won’t you please get it over right off because I’d like to go to the picnic with nothing on my mind.” “Picnic, indeed! You’ll go to no picnic today, Anne Shirley. That shall be your punishment. And it isn’t half severe enough either for what you’ve done!”
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉感到火热的怒火再次涌上心头。这个孩子拿走了她珍爱的紫水晶胸针，现在又丢了，现在平静地坐在那里，背诵着其中的细节，没有丝毫内疚或悔恨。 “安妮，这太可怕了，”她试图平静地说。 “你是我听说过的最邪恶的女孩。” “是的，我想是的。”安妮平静地表示同意。 “我知道我必须受到惩罚。惩罚我是你的责任，玛丽拉。你能不能马上把这件事结束，因为我想心无旁骛地去野餐。” “野餐，确实！你今天不能去野餐，安妮·雪莉。这将是对你的惩罚。而且对于你所做的事情来说，这还不够严厉！”

paragraphs.en: The retort silenced Matthew if it did not convince him. That dinner was a very dismal meal. The only cheerful thing about it was Jerry Buote, the hired boy, and Marilla resented his cheerfulness as a personal insult. When her dishes were washed and her bread sponge set and her hens fed Marilla remembered that she had noticed a small rent in her best black lace shawl when she had taken it off on Monday afternoon on returning from the Ladies’ Aid.
paragraphs.zh: 如果马修的反驳不能说服他的话，他就会闭嘴。那顿晚餐吃得非常惨淡。唯一令人高兴的是雇来的男孩杰里·博特，而玛丽拉则认为他的高兴是对他个人的侮辱。当她洗完盘子，准备好面包海绵，喂母鸡后，玛丽拉想起，周一下午从妇女救助会回来后，她把最好的黑色蕾丝披肩脱下来，发现它有一点小裂痕。

chapters.title: Chapter 15: A Tempest in the School Teapot
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 15 章：吉尔伯特叫“胡萝卜”引发冲突

paragraphs.en: WHAT a splendid day!” said Anne, drawing a long breath. “Isn’t it good just to be alive on a day like this? I pity the people who aren’t born yet for missing it. They may have good days, of course, but they can never have this one. And it’s splendider still to have such a lovely way to go to school by, isn’t it?” “It’s a lot nicer than going round by the road; that is so dusty and hot,” said Diana practically, peeping into her dinner basket and mentally calculating if the three juicy, toothsome, raspberry tarts reposing there were divided among ten girls how many bites each girl would have.
paragraphs.zh: 多么美好的一天啊！”安妮长长地吸了一口气说道。 “能在这样的日子里活着不是很好吗？我很遗憾那些还没有出生的人错过了它。当然，他们可能会有美好的日子，但他们永远不会有这样的日子。而且能有这么可爱的方式去上学，那真是太棒了，不是吗？” “这比在路边绕来绕去好多了；又脏又热。”黛安娜一边说，一边偷偷地看着她的餐篮，心里盘算着如果把放在那里的三个多汁、美味的覆盆子馅饼分给十个女孩，每个女孩会咬多少口。

paragraphs.en: “Nonsense,” said Diana, whose black eyes and glossy tresses had played such havoc with the hearts of Avonlea schoolboys that her name figured on the porch walls in half a dozen take-notices. “It’s only meant as a joke. And don’t you be too sure your name won’t ever be written up. Charlie Sloane is dead gone on you. He told his mother--his mother, mind you--that you were the smartest girl in school. That’s better than being good-looking.” “No, it isn’t,” said Anne, feminine to the core. “I’d rather be pretty than clever. And I hate Charlie Sloane, I can’t bear a boy with goggle eyes. If anyone wrote my name up with his I’d never get over it, Diana Barry. But it is nice to keep head of your class.”
paragraphs.zh: “胡说八道，”戴安娜说，她的黑眼睛和光泽的头发对埃文利学童的心造成了如此大的破坏，以至于她的名字出现在六张注意事项的门廊墙上。 “这只是个玩笑。你别太确定你的名字永远不会被写下来。查理·斯隆对你很着迷。他告诉他的母亲——他的母亲，请注意——你是学校里最聪明的女孩。这比长得漂亮要好。” “不，不是的，”安妮说道，语气里充满了女性气息。 “我宁愿漂亮，也不愿聪明。而且我讨厌查理·斯隆，我无法忍受一个长着护目镜的男孩。如果有人把我的名字和他的名字写在一起，我永远不会忘记，戴安娜·巴里。但在班上保持领先是件好事。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m awfully sorry I made fun of your hair, Anne,” he whispered contritely. “Honest I am. Don’t be mad for keeps, now.” Anne swept by disdainfully, without look or sign of hearing. “Oh how could you, Anne?” breathed Diana as they went down the road half reproachfully, half admiringly. Diana felt that she could never have resisted Gilbert’s plea. “I shall never forgive Gilbert Blythe,” said Anne firmly. “And Mr. Phillips spelled my name without an e, too. The iron has entered into my soul, Diana.” Diana hadn’t the least idea what Anne meant but she understood it was something terrible.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，我很抱歉我取笑了你的头发。”他悔恨地低声说道。 “我是诚实的。现在别生气了。”安妮轻蔑地掠过，看也不看，也没有听见。 “噢，安妮，你怎么能这样？”当他们走在路上时，戴安娜半是责备半是钦佩地喘着气。戴安娜觉得她永远无法抗拒吉尔伯特的恳求。 “我永远不会原谅吉尔伯特·布莱斯，”安妮坚定地说。 “菲利普斯先生也把我的名字拼写成没有e。戴安娜，铁已经进入了我的灵魂。”戴安娜根本不明白安妮的意思，但她知道这是一件可怕的事情。

paragraphs.en: “She’ll have to,” said Anne. “I’ll never go to school to that man again.” “Oh, Anne!” Diana looked as if she were ready to cry. “I do think you’re mean. What shall I do? Mr. Phillips will make me sit with that horrid Gertie Pye--I know he will because she is sitting alone. Do come back, Anne.” “I’d do almost anything in the world for you, Diana,” said Anne sadly. “I’d let myself be torn limb from limb if it would do you any good. But I can’t do this, so please don’t ask it. You harrow up my very soul.”
paragraphs.zh: “她必须这样做，”安妮说。 “我再也不会去那个男人的学校了。” “哦，安妮！”戴安娜看起来好像快要哭了。 “我确实认为你很卑鄙。我该怎么办？菲利普斯先生会让我和那个可怕的格蒂·派伊坐在一起——我知道他会的，因为她一个人坐着。一定要回来，安妮。” “我愿意为你做任何事情，戴安娜，”安妮悲伤地说。 “如果这对你有什么好处的话，我愿意让自己被撕成碎片。但我做不到，所以请不要问这个。你把我的灵魂都掏空了。”

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Diana is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 16 章：误拿红葡萄酒款待戴安娜

paragraphs.en: OCTOBER was a beautiful month at Green Gables, when the birches in the hollow turned as golden as sunshine and the maples behind the orchard were royal crimson and the wild cherry-trees along the lane put on the loveliest shades of dark red and bronzy green, while the fields sunned themselves in aftermaths. “Oh, Marilla,” she exclaimed one Saturday morning, coming dancing in with her arms full of gorgeous boughs, “I’m so glad I live in a world where there are Octobers. It would be terrible if we just skipped from September to November, wouldn’t it? Look at these maple branches. Don’t they give you a thrill--several thrills? I’m going to decorate my room with them.”
paragraphs.zh: 十月对绿山墙来说是一个美丽的月份，山谷里的白桦树变成了阳光般的金色，果园后面的枫树呈现出高贵的深红色，小巷两旁的野樱桃树呈现出最可爱的深红色和青铜绿色，而田野则在余波中沐浴在阳光下。 “哦，玛丽拉，”一个星期六的早晨，她抱着满是美丽树枝的舞蹈走进来，大声说道，“我很高兴我生活在一个有十月的世界。如果我们直接从九月跳到十一月，那就太可怕了，不是吗？看看这些枫树枝。它们难道不会给你带来刺激吗？我要用它们来装饰我的房间。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, ever so many,” said Anne forgetting to be dignified and jumping up quickly. “Let’s go out to the orchard and get some of the Red Sweetings, Diana. Marilla says we can have all that are left on the tree. Marilla is a very generous woman. She said we could have fruit cake and cherry preserves for tea. But it isn’t good manners to tell your company what you are going to give them to eat, so I won’t tell you what she said we could have to drink. Only it begins with an R and a C and it’s bright red color. I love bright red drinks, don’t you? They taste twice as good as any other color.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，真是太多了。”安妮忘记了尊严，飞快地跳了起来。 “戴安娜，我们去果园买一些红色糖果吧。玛丽拉说我们可以吃掉树上剩下的所有东西。玛丽拉是个非常慷慨的女人。她说我们可以吃水果蛋糕和樱桃蜜饯当茶。但是告诉你的公司你要给他们吃什么是不礼貌的，所以我不会告诉你她说我们可以喝什么。只是它以 R 和 C 开头，而且是鲜红色的。我你喜欢鲜红色的饮料，不是吗？它们的味道是其他颜色的两倍。”

paragraphs.en: “I never heard of company going home without tea,” she mourned. “Oh, Diana, do you suppose that it’s possible you’re really taking the smallpox? If you are I’ll go and nurse you, you can depend on that. I’ll never forsake you. But I do wish you’d stay till after tea. Where do you feel bad?” And indeed, she walked very dizzily. Anne, with tears of disappointment in her eyes, got Diana’s hat and went with her as far as the Barry yard fence. Then she wept all the way back to Green Gables, where she sorrowfully put the remainder of the raspberry cordial back into the pantry and got tea ready for Matthew and Jerry, with all the zest gone out of the performance.
paragraphs.zh: “我从来没有听说过有人不喝茶就回家，”她哀悼道。 “哦，黛安娜，你认为你真的可能得了天花吗？如果你真的得了天花，我会去护理你，你可以放心。我永远不会抛弃你。但我真希望你能留下来，直到喝完茶后。你哪里不舒服吗？”确实，她走得非常头晕。安妮眼里含着失望的泪水，拿起戴安娜的帽子，跟着她一直走到巴里院子的栅栏前。然后她一路哭着回到绿山墙，悲伤地把剩下的覆盆子甜酒放回食品储藏室，为马修和杰瑞准备茶，表演的所有热情都消失了。

paragraphs.en: “My courage fails me at the thought of facing Diana’s injured mother,” sighed Anne. “I wish you’d go, Marilla. You’re so much more dignified than I am. Likely she’d listen to you quicker than to me.” “Well, I will,” said Marilla, reflecting that it would probably be the wiser course. “Don’t cry any more, Anne. It will be all right.” Marilla had changed her mind about it being all right by the time she got back from Orchard Slope. Anne was watching for her coming and flew to the porch door to meet her. “Oh, Marilla, I know by your face that it’s been no use,” she said sorrowfully. “Mrs. Barry won’t forgive me?”
paragraphs.zh: “一想到要面对戴安娜受伤的母亲，我就失去了勇气，”安妮叹了口气。 “我希望你能走，玛丽拉。你比我有尊严得多。她可能会比我更快地听你的。” “好吧，我会的，”玛丽拉说，她认为这可能是更明智的做法。 “别再哭了，安妮。不会有事的。”当玛丽拉从果园坡回来时，她改变了主意，认为一切都好。安妮正在等待她的到来，飞奔到门廊门口迎接她。 “哦，玛丽拉，从你的表情我就知道这是没有用的，”她悲伤地说。 “巴里夫人不会原谅我吗？”

chapters.title: Chapter 17: A New Interest in Life
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 17 章：悲伤离别与重返校园

paragraphs.en: THE next afternoon Anne, bending over her patchwork at the kitchen window, happened to glance out and beheld Diana down by the Dryad’s Bubble beckoning mysteriously. In a trice Anne was out of the house and flying down to the hollow, astonishment and hope struggling in her expressive eyes. But the hope faded when she saw Diana’s dejected countenance. “No; and oh, Anne, she says I’m never to play with you again. I’ve cried and cried and I told her it wasn’t your fault, but it wasn’t any use. I had ever such a time coaxing her to let me come down and say good-bye to you. She said I was only to stay ten minutes and she’s timing me by the clock.”
paragraphs.zh: 第二天下午，安妮在厨房的窗户前弯下腰，看着她的拼布作品，碰巧向外瞥了一眼，看到戴安娜在树妖的泡泡旁边神秘地招手。刹那间，安妮走出了房子，飞向了空地，她那双富有​​表情的眼睛里充满了惊讶和希望。但当她看到戴安娜沮丧的表情时，希望破灭了。 “不；哦，安妮，她说我再也不会和你一起玩了。我哭了又哭，告诉她这不是你的错，但这没有任何用处。我曾经有一次哄她让我下来和你告别。她说我只待十分钟，她按照时钟给我计时。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes. I’ve got my patchwork scissors in my apron pocket fortunately,” said Anne. She solemnly clipped one of Diana’s curls. “Fare thee well, my beloved friend. Henceforth we must be as strangers though living side by side. But my heart will ever be faithful to thee.” Anne stood and watched Diana out of sight, mournfully waving her hand to the latter whenever she turned to look back. Then she returned to the house, not a little consoled for the time being by this romantic parting.
paragraphs.zh: “是的。幸运的是，我的围裙口袋里有我的拼布剪刀，”安妮说。她郑重地剪掉了戴安娜的一头卷发。 “再见了，我亲爱的朋友。从此我们虽然毗邻而居，却像陌生人一样。但我的心永远忠于你。”安妮站在那里，看着戴安娜消失在视线中，每当她回头看时，她都会悲伤地向后者挥手。然后她回到了家，暂时没有因为这次浪漫的离别而感到一点安慰。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll try to be a model pupil,” agreed Anne dolefully. “There won’t be much fun in it, I expect. Mr. Phillips said Minnie Andrews was a model pupil and there isn’t a spark of imagination or life in her. She is just dull and poky and never seems to have a good time. But I feel so depressed that perhaps it will come easy to me now. I’m going round by the road. I couldn’t bear to go by the Birch Path all alone. I should weep bitter tears if I did.”
paragraphs.zh: “我会努力成为一名模范学生。”安妮悲伤地同意道。 “我想这不会有太多乐趣。菲利普斯先生说米妮·安德鲁斯是个模范学生，她身上没有一点想象力和生命力。她只是迟钝、狭隘，似乎从来没有过得开心。但我感到很沮丧，也许现在对我来说会很容易。我正在路边转。我不忍心独自走在桦树小路上。如果我这样做了，我应该流下痛苦的眼泪。”

paragraphs.en: “Diana might just have smiled at me once, I think,” she mourned to Marilla that night. But the next morning a note most fearfully and wonderfully twisted and folded, and a small parcel were passed across to Anne. “Dear Anne, ran the former, “Mother says I’m not to play with you or talk to you even in school. It isn’t my fault and don’t be cross at me, because I love you as much as ever. I miss you awfully to tell all my secrets to and I don’t like Gertie Pye one bit. I made you one of the new bookmarkers out of red tissue paper. They are awfully fashionable now and only three girls in school know how to make them. When you look at it remember
paragraphs.zh: “我想，戴安娜可能只是对我微笑过一次，”那天晚上她向玛丽拉哀悼。但第二天早上，一张纸条被极其可怕地、奇妙地扭曲和折叠，还有一个小包裹被传递给了安妮。 “亲爱的安妮，”前者说道，“妈妈说即使在学校我也不会和你一起玩或说话。这不是我的错，不要生我的气，因为我一如既往地爱你。我非常想念你告诉我所有的秘密，而且我一点也不喜欢格蒂·派伊。我用红色薄纸给你做了一个新书签。它们现在非常流行，学校里只有三个女孩知道如何制作它们。当你看到它的时候记得

chapters.title: Chapter 18: Anne to the Rescue
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 18 章：救治喉喉急症与友情恢复

paragraphs.en: ALL things great are wound up with all things little. At first glance it might not seem that the decision of a certain Canadian Premier to include Prince Edward Island in a political tour could have much or anything to do with the fortunes of little Anne Shirley at Green Gables. But it had.
paragraphs.zh: 所有伟大的事情都与所有小事情有关。乍一看，加拿大某位总理将爱德华王子岛纳入政治访问的决定似乎与绿山墙小安妮·雪莉的命运没有多大关系。但确实如此。

paragraphs.en: “Well, I suppose I must finish up my lessons. I won’t allow myself to open that new book Jane lent me until I’m through. But it’s a terrible temptation, Matthew. Even when I turn my back on it I can see it there just as plain. Jane said she cried herself sick over it. I love a book that makes me cry. But I think I’ll carry that book into the sitting room and lock it in the jam closet and give you the key. And you must not give it to me, Matthew, until my lessons are done, not even if I implore you on my bended knees. It’s all very well to say resist temptation, but it’s ever so much easier to resist it if you can’t get the key. And then shall I run down the cellar and get some russets, Matthew? Wouldn’t you like some russets?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我想我必须完成我的课程。在我读完之前，我不会允许自己打开简借给我的那本新书。但这是一个可怕的诱惑，马修。即使我背对着它，我也能清楚地看到它在那里。简说她为此哭得很厉害。我喜欢一本让我哭泣的书。但我想我会把那本书带到客厅，把它锁在果酱柜里，然后把钥匙给你。你不可以把它给我，马修，在我的课程完成之前，即使我跪着恳求你，说抵制诱惑也很好，但如果你拿不到钥匙，那么抵制它会容易得多，马修，你不想要一些赤褐色吗？

paragraphs.en: “Minnie May has croup all right; she’s pretty bad, but I’ve seen them worse. First we must have lots of hot water. I declare, Diana, there isn’t more than a cupful in the kettle! There, I’ve filled it up, and, Mary Joe, you may put some wood in the stove. I don’t want to hurt your feelings but it seems to me you might have thought of this before if you’d any imagination. Now, I’ll undress Minnie May and put her to bed and you try to find some soft flannel cloths, Diana. I’m going to give her a dose of ipecac first of all.”
paragraphs.zh: “米妮·梅确实有哮吼，她很严重，但我见过更严重的。首先我们必须有很多热水。我宣布，戴安娜，水壶里已经没有超过一杯了！好了，我已经把它装满了，玛丽·乔，你可以在炉子里放一些木头。我不想伤害你的感情，但在我看来，如果你有想象力的话，你可能以前就想到过这一点。现在，我要脱掉米妮·梅的衣服，把她放进去。上床睡觉，你试着找一些柔软的法兰绒布，戴安娜，我首先要给她一剂吐根。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, he never got to be Premier on account of his looks,” said Marilla. “Such a nose as that man had! But he can speak. I was proud of being a Conservative. Rachel Lynde, of course, being a Liberal, had no use for him. Your dinner is in the oven, Anne, and you can get yourself some blue plum preserve out of the pantry. I guess you’re hungry. Matthew has been telling me about last night. I must say it was fortunate you knew what to do. I wouldn’t have had any idea myself, for I never saw a case of croup. There now, never mind talking till you’ve had your dinner. I can tell by the look of you that you’re just full up with speeches, but they’ll keep.”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，他从来没有因为他的外表而成为总理，”马里拉说。 “那个人有这样的鼻子！但他会说话。我为自己是一名保守党人而感到自豪。当然，雷切尔·林德，作为一名自由党人，对他没有用处。你的晚餐在烤箱里，安妮，你可以从食品储藏室里给自己买一些蓝李子蜜饯。我猜你饿了。马修一直在告诉我昨晚的事。我必须说，幸运的是你知道该怎么做。我自己也不知道，因为我从来没有见过一例好了，吃完晚饭之前别介意说话，从你的表情来看，你已经讲完了，但他们会继续讲下去的。”

chapters.title: Chapter 19: A Concert, a Catastrophe and a Confession
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 19 章：跳床意外与约瑟芬姑妈

paragraphs.en: MARILLA, can I go over to see Diana just for a minute?” asked Anne, running breathlessly down from the east gable one February evening. “I don’t see what you want to be traipsing about after dark for,” said Marilla shortly. “You and Diana walked home from school together and then stood down there in the snow for half an hour more, your tongues going the whole blessed time, clickety-clack. So I don’t think you’re very badly off to see her again.” “But she wants to see me,” pleaded Anne. “She has something very important to tell me.”
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉，我可以过去看看戴安娜吗？”二月的一个晚上，安妮气喘吁吁地从东山墙跑下来，问道。 “我不明白你想在天黑后闲逛做什么，”玛丽拉简短地说。 “你和戴安娜一起从学校走回家，然后在雪地里又站了半个小时，你们的舌头在整个受祝福的时间里都在说着咔哒声。所以我认为你再次见到她不会太糟糕。” “但她想见我，”安妮恳求道。 “她有很重要的事情要告诉我。”

paragraphs.en: “You’d think I ought to let Anne go to the moon if she took the notion, I’ve no doubt,” was Marilla’s amiable rejoinder. “I might have let her spend the night with Diana, if that was all. But I don’t approve of this concert plan. She’d go there and catch cold like as not, and have her head filled up with nonsense and excitement. It would unsettle her for a week. I understand that child’s disposition and what’s good for it better than you, Matthew.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果安妮接受这个想法，你会认为我应该让她去月球，我毫不怀疑，”马里拉和蔼可亲地反驳道。 “如果仅此而已，我可能会让她和戴安娜一起过夜。但我不赞成这个音乐会计划。她去那里会像不感冒一样，脑子里充满了胡言乱语和兴奋。这会让她不安一个星期。我比你更了解那个孩子的性格和好处，马修。”

paragraphs.en: Anne and Diana were never able to tell just how they got off that bed and out of the room. They only knew that after one frantic rush they found themselves tiptoeing shiveringly upstairs. “Oh, who was it--what was it?” whispered Anne, her teeth chattering with cold and fright. “It was Aunt Josephine,” said Diana, gasping with laughter. “Oh, Anne, it was Aunt Josephine, however she came to be there. Oh, and I know she will be furious. It’s dreadful--it’s really dreadful--but did you ever know anything so funny, Anne?”
paragraphs.zh: 安妮和戴安娜始终无法说出她们是如何从床上下来并走出房间的。他们只知道，一阵疯狂的冲刺之后，他们发现自己颤抖着蹑手蹑脚地上了楼。 “哦，那是谁——那是什么？”安妮小声说道，她的牙齿因寒冷和恐惧而打颤。 “是约瑟芬姨妈，”戴安娜笑着说道。 “哦，安妮，那是约瑟芬姨妈，不管她是怎么来的。哦，我知道她会生气的。这太可怕了——真的太可怕了——但是你知道有什么这么有趣的事吗，安妮？”

paragraphs.en: With this encouragement Anne bearded the lion in its den--that is to say, walked resolutely up to the sitting-room door and knocked faintly. A sharp “Come in” followed. Miss Josephine Barry, thin, prim, and rigid, was knitting fiercely by the fire, her wrath quite unappeased and her eyes snapping through her gold-rimmed glasses. She wheeled around in her chair, expecting to see Diana, and beheld a white-faced girl whose great eyes were brimmed up with a mixture of desperate courage and shrinking terror. “I’m Anne of Green Gables,” said the small visitor tremulously, clasping her hands with her characteristic gesture, “and I’ve come to confess, if you please.”
paragraphs.zh: 在这种鼓励下，安妮把狮子带进了洞里——也就是说，她坚定地走到客厅的门前，轻轻地敲了敲门。随后是一声尖锐的“请进”。约瑟芬·巴里小姐身材瘦小，拘谨而僵硬，她正在火边拼命地织毛衣，她的怒火丝毫没有平息，她的眼睛透过金框眼镜猛地瞪着。她在椅子上转过身来，期待见到戴安娜，却看到了一个白脸女孩，她的大眼睛里充满了绝望的勇气和畏缩的恐惧。 “我是绿山墙的安妮，”小访客颤抖着说道，用她特有的姿势握紧双手，“如果您愿意的话，我是来坦白的。”

chapters.title: Chapter 20: A Good Imagination Gone Wrong
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 20 章：鬼怪森林的想象恐慌

paragraphs.en: SPRING had come once more to Green Gables--the beautiful capricious, reluctant Canadian spring, lingering along through April and May in a succession of sweet, fresh, chilly days, with pink sunsets and miracles of resurrection and growth. The maples in Lover’s Lane were red budded and little curly ferns pushed up around the Dryad’s Bubble. Away up in the barrens, behind Mr. Silas Sloane’s place, the Mayflowers blossomed out, pink and white stars of sweetness under their brown leaves. All the school girls and boys had one golden afternoon gathering them, coming home in the clear, echoing twilight with arms and baskets full of flowery spoil.
paragraphs.zh: 春天再次来到了绿山墙——美丽的、反复无常的、不情愿的加拿大春天，在四月和五月中持续存在，伴随着一系列甜蜜、新鲜、寒冷的日子，伴随着粉红色的日落和复活和生长的奇迹。情人巷里的枫树已经发出了红色的芽，树妖泡泡周围长满了卷曲的小蕨类植物。在塞拉斯·斯隆先生住所后面的贫瘠之地，五月花绽放，棕色的叶子下绽放着粉色和白色的甜蜜星星。所有的男女学生都度过了一个金色的下午，他们在晴朗的暮色中带着手臂和装满鲜花的篮子回家。

paragraphs.en: “I guess you did your part in attending to the work and letting me rest,” said Marilla. “You seem to have got on fairly well and made fewer mistakes than usual. Of course it wasn’t exactly necessary to starch Matthew’s handkerchiefs! And most people when they put a pie in the oven to warm up for dinner take it out and eat it when it gets hot instead of leaving it to be burned to a crisp. But that doesn’t seem to be your way evidently.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想你尽了自己的一份力，专注于工作并让我休息，”马里拉说。 “你似乎相处得很好，犯的错误也比平时少了。当然，没必要给马修的手帕上浆！而且大多数人把馅饼放进烤箱加热准备晚餐时，都会在热的时候拿出来吃，而不是让它烤得酥脆。但这显然不是你的作风。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll have to go around by the road, then,” said Anne, taking up her hat reluctantly. “Go by the road and waste half an hour! I’d like to catch you!” “The Haunted Wood! Are you crazy? What under the canopy is the Haunted Wood?” “Fiddlesticks! There is no such thing as a haunted wood anywhere. Who has been telling you such stuff?”
paragraphs.zh: “那我就得绕路走了。”安妮不情愿地拿起帽子说道。 “沿着路走，浪费半个小时！我想抓住你！” “鬼林！你疯了吗？天篷下面是什么鬼林？” “胡说八道！世界上根本不存在闹鬼的树林。谁告诉你这些事的？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, but there are, Marilla,” cried Anne eagerly. “I know people who have seen them. And they are respectable people. Charlie Sloane says that his grandmother saw his grandfather driving home the cows one night after he’d been buried for a year. You know Charlie Sloane’s grandmother wouldn’t tell a story for anything. She’s a very religious woman. And Mrs. Thomas’s father was pursued home one night by a lamb of fire with its head cut off hanging by a strip of skin. He said he knew it was the spirit of his brother and that it was a warning he would die within nine days. He didn’t, but he died two years after, so you see it was really true. And Ruby Gillis says--”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，但是有，玛丽拉，”安妮急切地喊道。 “我认识一些见过它们的人。他们都是受人尊敬的人。查理·斯隆说，他的祖母在他被埋葬一年后，有一天晚上看到他的祖父赶着牛回家。你知道查理·斯隆的祖母不会讲任何故事。她是一个非常虔诚的女人。托马斯夫人的父亲有一天晚上被一只火焰羔羊追赶回家，它的头被一条皮割下来。他说他知道那是他哥哥的灵魂，那是一个警告他会在九天内死去，但他没有，但两年后他就去世了，所以你看，鲁比·吉利斯说的是真的——”

chapters.title: Chapter 21: A New Departure in Flavorings
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 21 章：把止痛药当香精做蛋糕

paragraphs.en: DEAR me, there is nothing but meetings and partings in this world, as Mrs. Lynde says,” remarked Anne plaintively, putting her slate and books down on the kitchen table on the last day of June and wiping her red eyes with a very damp handkerchief. “Wasn’t it fortunate, Marilla, that I took an extra handkerchief to school today? I had a presentiment that it would be needed.” “I never thought you were so fond of Mr. Phillips that you’d require two handkerchiefs to dry your tears just because he was going away,” said Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: 亲爱的我，正如林德夫人所说，这个世界上只有相遇和离别，”六月的最后一天，安妮哀怨地说，她把石板和书放在厨房的桌子上，用一块湿漉漉的手帕擦着红红的眼睛。“玛丽拉，我今天多带了一块手帕去学校，这不是很幸运吗？我有一种预感，这是需要的。” “我没想到你这么喜欢菲利普斯先生，只因为他要走了，你就需要两块手帕来擦干眼泪，”玛丽拉说。

paragraphs.en: “Everything is ready, Diana, except my cake which I’m to make in the morning, and the baking-powder biscuits which Marilla will make just before teatime. I assure you, Diana, that Marilla and I have had a busy two days of it. It’s such a responsibility having a minister’s family to tea. I never went through such an experience before. You should just see our pantry. It’s a sight to behold. We’re going to have jellied chicken and cold tongue. We’re to have two kinds of jelly, red and yellow, and whipped cream and lemon pie, and cherry pie, and three kinds of cookies, and fruit cake, and Marilla’s famous yellow plum preserves that she keeps especially for ministers, and pound cake and layer cake, and biscuits as aforesaid; and new bread and old both, in case the minister is dyspeptic and can’t eat new. Mrs. Lynde says ministers are dyspeptic, but I don’t think Mr. Allan has been a minister long enough for it to have had a bad effect on him. I just grow cold when I think of my layer cake. Oh, Diana, what if it shouldn’t be good! I dreamed last night that I was chased all around by a fearful goblin with a big layer cake for a head.”
paragraphs.zh: “一切都准备好了，戴安娜，除了我早上要做的蛋糕，还有玛丽拉在下午茶时间之前做的发酵粉饼干。我向你保证，戴安娜，我和玛丽拉已经忙了两天了。请牧师的家人喝茶真是一种责任。我以前从来没有经历过这样的经历。你应该看看我们的食品储藏室。那是一个值得一看的景象。我们要吃鸡肉冻和冷饮。我们要吃两种果冻，红色和黄色，鲜奶油和柠檬派，樱桃派，三种饼干，水果蛋糕，还有玛丽拉专门为部长们保留的著名的黄李子蜜饯，还有前面提到的磅蛋糕和夹心饼干；还有新面包和旧面包，以防部长消化不良，林德夫人说部长消化不良，但我不吃。艾伦先生当牧师已经够久了，这对他产生了不好的影响，哦，戴安娜，如果它不好吃怎么办？昨晚我梦见我被一个头戴大蛋糕的可怕妖精追赶。

paragraphs.en: “It’s Anne’s doings,” said Marilla, grimly just; and Anne felt that Mrs. Allan’s approving smile was almost too much happiness for this world. Matthew was there, having been inveigled into the party only goodness and Anne knew how. He had been in such a state of shyness and nervousness that Marilla had given him up in despair, but Anne took him in hand so successfully that he now sat at the table in his best clothes and white collar and talked to the minister not uninterestingly. He never said a word to Mrs. Allan, but that perhaps was not to be expected. All went merry as a marriage bell until Anne’s layer cake was passed. Mrs. Allan, having already been helped to a bewildering variety, declined it. But Marilla, seeing the disappointment on Anne’s face, said smilingly:
paragraphs.zh: “这是安妮干的，”玛丽拉严肃地说。安妮觉得艾伦夫人赞许的微笑对于这个世界来说简直是太幸福了。马修也在场，他只是被善意地骗进了聚会，而安妮也知道是怎么回事。他一直处于如此害羞和紧张的状态，以至于玛丽拉绝望地放弃了他，但安妮成功地抓住了他，以至于他现在穿着最好的衣服和白领坐在桌旁，与部长交谈起来并不无趣。他从未对艾伦夫人说过一句话，但这也许是出乎意料的。一切都像结婚的钟声一样欢乐，直到安妮的夹心蛋糕被递过去。艾伦夫人已经被帮助做了一些令人眼花缭乱的事情，所以拒绝了。但玛丽拉看到安妮脸上的失望，微笑道：

paragraphs.en: “I couldn’t--I had such a cold!” and with this she fairly fled to the gable chamber, where she cast herself on the bed and wept as one who refuses to be comforted. Presently a light step sounded on the stairs and somebody entered the room.
paragraphs.zh: “我不能——我感冒了！”说完，她就逃到了山墙房间，倒在床上，哭了起来，就像一个不肯接受安慰的人。不一会儿，楼梯上响起了轻微的脚步声，有人走进了房间。

chapters.title: Chapter 22: Anne is Invited Out to Tea
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 22 章：牧师家的愉快下午茶

paragraphs.en: AND what are your eyes popping out of your head about. Now?” asked Marilla, when Anne had just come in from a run to the post office. “Have you discovered another kindred spirit?” Excitement hung around Anne like a garment, shone in her eyes, kindled in every feature. She had come dancing up the lane, like a wind-blown sprite, through the mellow sunshine and lazy shadows of the August evening. “No, Marilla, but oh, what do you think? I am invited to tea at the manse tomorrow afternoon! Mrs. Allan left the letter for me at the post office. Just look at it, Marilla. ‘Miss Anne Shirley, Green Gables.’ That is the first time I was ever called ‘Miss.’ Such a thrill as it gave me! I shall cherish it forever among my choicest treasures.”
paragraphs.zh: 还有你的眼睛在想什么？现在？”当安妮刚从邮局跑步回来时，玛丽拉问道。 “你有发现另一个志同道合的人吗？”兴奋像一件衣服一样笼罩着安妮，在她的眼睛里闪闪发光，每一个特征都被点燃。她像一个被风吹动的精灵，穿过八月傍晚柔和的阳光和慵懒的阴影，沿着小巷翩翩起舞。 “不，玛丽拉，但是哦，你觉得怎么样？明天下午我被邀请去庄园喝茶！艾伦夫人把这封信留在了邮局给我。看看它，玛丽拉。 “绿山墙的安妮·雪莉小姐。”这是我第一次被称为“小姐”。这让我非常兴奋！我将把它永远珍藏在我最珍贵的珍宝中。”

paragraphs.en: For Anne to take things calmly would have been to change her nature. All “spirit and fire and dew,” as she was, the pleasures and pains of life came to her with trebled intensity. Marilla felt this and was vaguely troubled over it, realizing that the ups and downs of existence would probably bear hardly on this impulsive soul and not sufficiently understanding that the equally great capacity for delight might more than compensate. Therefore Marilla conceived it to be her duty to drill Anne into a tranquil uniformity of disposition as impossible and alien to her as to a dancing sunbeam in one of the brook shallows. She did not make much headway, as she sorrowfully admitted to herself. The downfall of some dear hope or plan plunged Anne into “deeps of affliction.” The fulfillment thereof exalted her to dizzy realms of delight. Marilla had almost begun to despair of ever fashioning this waif of the world into her model little girl of demure manners and prim deportment. Neither would she have believed that she really liked Anne much better as she was.
paragraphs.zh: 对安妮来说，冷静地对待事情就等于改变了她的本性。所有的“精神、火和露水”，就像她一样，生活中的快乐和痛苦以三倍的强度降临到她身上。玛丽拉感觉到了这一点，并隐约感到困扰，意识到生活的起起落落可能对这个冲动的灵魂来说很难承受，但她没有充分理解同样强大的快乐能力可能会弥补这一点。因此，玛丽拉认为，她有责任让安妮养成一种平静、统一的性格，这对她来说是不可能的，也是陌生的，就像小溪浅滩上舞动的阳光一样。正如她悲伤地向自己承认的那样，她并没有取得多大进展。一些美好的希望或计划的破灭使安妮陷入了“痛苦的深渊”。这一愿望的实现使她欣喜若狂。玛丽拉几乎开始对把这个世界上的流浪儿塑造成举止端庄、举止拘谨的模范小女孩感到绝望。她也不会相信她真的更喜欢安妮。

paragraphs.en: “The trouble with you, Anne, is that you’re thinking too much about yourself. You should just think of Mrs. Allan and what would be nicest and most agreeable to her,” said Marilla, hitting for once in her life on a very sound and pithy piece of advice. Anne instantly realized this. “You are right, Marilla. I’ll try not to think about myself at all.” Anne evidently got through her visit without any serious breach of “etiquette,” for she came home through the twilight, under a great, high-sprung sky gloried over with trails of saffron and rosy cloud, in a beatified state of mind and told Marilla all about it happily, sitting on the big red-sandstone slab at the kitchen door with her tired curly head in Marilla’s gingham lap.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你的问题在于你想得太多了。你应该只想到艾伦太太，想想什么对她来说是最好、最舒服的，”玛丽拉说，她一生中第一次提出了一个非常合理和简洁的建议。安妮立刻意识到了这一点。 “你是对的，玛丽拉。我会尽量不去想我自己。”安妮显然没有严重违反“礼节”，因为她在暮色中回到家，在一片藏红花和玫瑰色云彩映照下的伟大高耸天空下，带着幸福的心情，高兴地告诉玛丽拉这一切，坐在厨房门口的大红砂岩板上，疲惫的卷发头枕在玛丽拉的格子腿上。

paragraphs.en: Anne evidently got through her visit without any serious breach of “etiquette,” for she came home through the twilight, under a great, high-sprung sky gloried over with trails of saffron and rosy cloud, in a beatified state of mind and told Marilla all about it happily, sitting on the big red-sandstone slab at the kitchen door with her tired curly head in Marilla’s gingham lap. A cool wind was blowing down over the long harvest fields from the rims of firry western hills and whistling through the poplars. One clear star hung over the orchard and the fireflies were flitting over in Lover’s Lane, in and out among the ferns and rustling boughs. Anne watched them as she talked and somehow felt that wind and stars and fireflies were all tangled up together into something unutterably sweet and enchanting.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮显然没有严重违反“礼节”，因为她在暮色中回到家，在一片藏红花和玫瑰色云彩映照下的伟大高耸天空下，带着幸福的心情，高兴地告诉玛丽拉这一切，坐在厨房门口的大红砂岩板上，疲惫的卷发头枕在玛丽拉的格子腿上。一阵凉爽的风从西部冷杉山的边缘吹过长长的收割田，呼啸着穿过白杨树。一颗清澈的星星悬挂在果园上空，萤火虫在情人巷飞过，在蕨类植物和沙沙作响的树枝间穿梭。安妮看着他们说话，不知怎的，感觉风、星星、萤火虫都纠缠在一起，组成了一种说不出的甜蜜和迷人。

chapters.title: Chapter 23: Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 23 章：屋顶走挑战与脚踝骨折

paragraphs.en: ANNE had to live through more than two weeks, as it happened. Almost a month having elapsed since the liniment cake episode, it was high time for her to get into fresh trouble of some sort, little mistakes, such as absentmindedly emptying a pan of skim milk into a basket of yarn balls in the pantry instead of into the pigs’ bucket, and walking clean over the edge of the log bridge into the brook while wrapped in imaginative reverie, not really being worth counting. A week after the tea at the manse Diana Barry gave a party. “Small and select,” Anne assured Marilla. “Just the girls in our class.”
paragraphs.zh: 碰巧，安妮不得不熬过两个多星期。搽剂糕事件过去快一个月了，她又要遇到新的麻烦了，一些小错误，比如心不在焉地把一锅脱脂牛奶倒进储藏室里的一篮子毛线球里，而不是倒进猪桶里，或者带着幻想从独木桥边走入小溪里，实在不值一提。戴安娜·巴里在庄园喝茶一周后举办了一场聚会。 “小而精选，”安妮向玛丽拉保证。 “就我们班的女生。”

paragraphs.en: “Then I dare you to do it,” said Josie defiantly. “I dare you to climb up there and walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry’s kitchen roof.” Anne turned pale, but there was clearly only one thing to be done. She walked toward the house, where a ladder was leaning against the kitchen roof. All the fifth-class girls said, “Oh!” partly in excitement, partly in dismay. “Don’t you do it, Anne,” entreated Diana. “You’ll fall off and be killed. Never mind Josie Pye. It isn’t fair to dare anybody to do anything so dangerous.” “I must do it. My honor is at stake,” said Anne solemnly. “I shall walk that ridgepole, Diana, or perish in the attempt. If I am killed you are to have my pearl bead ring.”
paragraphs.zh: “那我就挑战你这么做，”乔西挑衅地说。 “我敢说你敢爬上去，走在巴里先生厨房屋顶的屋脊上。”安妮脸色惨白，但显然只有一件事要做。她朝房子走去，厨房的屋顶上斜靠着一架梯子。五年级的女生们齐声“哦！”一半是兴奋，一半是沮丧。 “你别这么做，安妮，”戴安娜恳求道。 “你会摔下来并被杀。别介意乔西·派伊。敢于让任何人做如此危险的事情是不公平的。” “我必须这么做。我的荣誉受到威胁。”安妮严肃地说。 “戴安娜，我将走过那根屋脊，否则就会丧命。如果我被杀，你将得到我的珍珠戒指。”

paragraphs.en: “Where?” sobbed Carrie Sloane. “Oh, where, Anne?” Before Anne could answer Mrs. Barry appeared on the scene. At sight of her Anne tried to scramble to her feet, but sank back again with a sharp little cry of pain. “My ankle,” gasped Anne. “Oh, Diana, please find your father and ask him to take me home. I know I can never walk there. And I’m sure I couldn’t hop so far on one foot when Jane couldn’t even hop around the garden.” Marilla was out in the orchard picking a panful of summer apples when she saw Mr. Barry coming over the log bridge and up the slope, with Mrs. Barry beside him and a whole procession of little girls trailing after him. In his arms he carried Anne, whose head lay limply against his shoulder.
