paragraphs.zh: “在哪里？”嘉莉·斯隆抽泣着。 “哦，安妮，去哪儿？”安妮还没来得及回答，巴里夫人就出现了。安妮一看到她，就想爬起来，但又因疼痛而发出一声尖锐的小叫声，又倒了回去。 “我的脚踝，”安妮喘着气说。 “哦，戴安娜，请找到你的父亲，请他带我回家。我知道我永远无法走到那里。而且我确信，当简甚至无法在花园里跳来跳去时，我也无法用一只脚跳那么远。”玛丽拉正在果园里采摘一盘夏季苹果，这时她看到巴里先生走过独木桥，爬上了斜坡，巴里太太在他身边，一队小女孩跟在他后面。他怀里抱着安妮，安妮的头无力地靠在他的肩膀上。

paragraphs.en: “It was your own fault,” said Marilla, twitching down the blind and lighting a lamp. “And that is just why you should be sorry for me,” said Anne, “because the thought that it is all my own fault is what makes it so hard. If I could blame it on anybody I would feel so much better. But what would you have done, Marilla, if you had been dared to walk a ridgepole?” “I’d have stayed on good firm ground and let them dare away. Such absurdity!” said Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: “这是你自己的错。”玛丽拉拉下百叶窗，点着一盏灯说道。 “这就是为什么你应该为我感到难过，”安妮说，“因为一想到这一切都是我自己的错，那就让事情变得如此困难。如果我能把这一切归咎于任何人，我会感觉好多了。但是，玛丽拉，如果你敢于走上屋脊，你会怎么做呢？” “我会站在坚实的地面上，让他们胆敢离开。这真是荒谬！”玛丽拉说。

chapters.title: Chapter 24: Miss Stacy and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 24 章：斯泰西老师与音乐会

paragraphs.en: IT was October again when Anne was ready to go back to school--a glorious October, all red and gold, with mellow mornings when the valleys were filled with delicate mists as if the spirit of autumn had poured them in for the sun to drain--amethyst, pearl, silver, rose, and smoke-blue. The dews were so heavy that the fields glistened like cloth of silver and there were such heaps of rustling leaves in the hollows of many-stemmed woods to run crisply through. The Birch Path was a canopy of yellow and the ferns were sear and brown all along it. There was a tang in the very air that inspired the hearts of small maidens tripping, unlike snails, swiftly and willingly to school; and it was jolly to be back again at the little brown desk beside Diana, with Ruby Gillis nodding across the aisle and Carrie Sloane sending up notes and Julia Bell passing a “chew” of gum down from the back seat. Anne drew a long breath of happiness as she sharpened her pencil and arranged her picture cards in her desk. Life was certainly very interesting.
paragraphs.zh: 又到了十月，安妮准备回学校了——一个光荣的十月，一切都是红色和金色，早晨是柔和的，山谷中弥漫着淡淡的薄雾，仿佛秋天的精灵把它们倾注进来，让阳光排出——紫水晶色、珍珠色、银色、玫瑰色和烟蓝色。露水如此浓重，田野像银布一样闪闪发光，多茎树林的空洞里有一堆堆沙沙作响的树叶，清脆地穿过。白桦林小径是一片黄色的树冠，沿途的蕨类植物都是焦黄的。空气中弥漫着一股腥味，激发了小姑娘们的心，不像蜗牛，迅速而心甘情愿地去上学；再次回到戴安娜身边的棕色小桌子旁真是令人高兴，鲁比·吉利斯在过道对面点头，凯莉·斯隆发来便条，朱莉娅·贝尔从后座上递下一块“嚼”口香糖。安妮幸福地长长地吸了一口气，削尖了铅笔，把画卡放在书桌上。生活当然非常有趣。

paragraphs.en: “Of course I will,” said Anne meditatively, “but I won’t be able to do it so well, I know. It won’t be so exciting as it is when you have a whole schoolful before you hanging breathlessly on your words. I know I won’t be able to make your blood run cold.” “Mrs. Lynde says it made her blood run cold to see the boys climbing to the very tops of those big trees on Bell’s hill after crows’ nests last Friday,” said Marilla. “I wonder at Miss Stacy for encouraging it.” “But we wanted a crow’s nest for nature study,” explained Anne. “That was on our field afternoon. Field afternoons are splendid, Marilla. And Miss Stacy explains everything so beautifully. We have to write compositions on our field afternoons and I write the best ones.”
paragraphs.zh: “我当然会，”安妮若有所思地说，“但我知道，我不会做得那么好。在你气喘吁吁地坚持自己的话之前，它不会像整个学校那样令人兴奋。我知道我无法让你热血沸腾。” “林德夫人说，上周五看到孩子们在鸟巢后爬到贝尔山上那些大树的最高处，让她感到心寒，”马里拉说。 “我对史黛西小姐的鼓励感到好奇。” “但我们想要一个用于自然研究的瞭望台，”安妮解释道。 “那是在我们的野外下午。野外下午真是太棒了，玛丽拉。史黛西小姐把一切都解释得那么漂亮。我们必须在野外下午写作文，而我写的最好。”

paragraphs.en: “But she did say it, Marilla. And indeed I’m not vain about it. How can I be, when I’m such a dunce at geometry? Although I’m really beginning to see through it a little, too. Miss Stacy makes it so clear. Still, I’ll never be good at it and I assure you it is a humbling reflection. But I love writing compositions. Mostly Miss Stacy lets us choose our own subjects; but next week we are to write a composition on some remarkable person. It’s hard to choose among so many remarkable people who have lived. Mustn’t it be splendid to be remarkable and have compositions written about you after you’re dead? Oh, I would dearly love to be remarkable. I think when I grow up I’ll be a trained nurse and go with the Red Crosses to the field of battle as a messenger of mercy. That is, if I don’t go out as a foreign missionary. That would be very romantic, but one would have to be very good to be a missionary, and that would be a stumbling block. We have physical culture exercises every day, too. They make you graceful and promote digestion.”
paragraphs.zh: “但她确实这么说过，玛丽拉。事实上，我对此并不自负。当我在几何学上这么笨的时候，我怎么能这样呢？虽然我也确实开始有点看透它了。史黛西小姐说得很清楚。不过，我永远不会擅长它，我向你保证，这是一个令人谦卑的反思。但我喜欢写作文。史黛西小姐大多让我们选择自己的主题；但下周我们要写一篇关于某个杰出人物的作文。它是在这么多活着的杰出人物中，很难做出选择，难道不是很出色吗？哦，我非常想成为一名受过训练的护士，并作为仁慈的使者与红十字会一起去战场，那将是非常浪漫的，但一个人必须成为一名传教士。我们每天都会进行体育锻炼，它们可以让你变得优雅并促进消化。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, when you can combine patriotism and fun, isn’t it all right? Of course it’s real nice to be getting up a concert. We’re going to have six choruses and Diana is to sing a solo. I’m in two dialogues--‘The Society for the Suppression of Gossip’ and ‘The Fairy Queen.’ The boys are going to have a dialogue too. And I’m to have two recitations, Marilla. I just tremble when I think of it, but it’s a nice thrilly kind of tremble. And we’re to have a tableau at the last--‘Faith, Hope and Charity.’ Diana and Ruby and I are to be in it, all draped in white with flowing hair. I’m to be Hope, with my hands clasped--so--and my eyes uplifted. I’m going to practice my recitations in the garret. Don’t be alarmed if you hear me groaning. I have to groan heartrendingly in one of them, and it’s really hard to get up a good artistic groan, Marilla. Josie Pye is sulky because she didn’t get the part she wanted in the dialogue. She wanted to be the fairy queen. That would have been ridiculous, for who ever heard of a fairy queen as fat as Josie? Fairy queens must be slender. Jane Andrews is to be the queen and I am to be one of her maids of honor. Josie says she thinks a red-haired fairy is just as ridiculous as a fat one, but I do not let myself mind what Josie says. I’m to have a wreath of white roses on my hair and Ruby Gillis is going to lend me her slippers because I haven’t any of my own. It’s necessary for fairies to have slippers, you know. You couldn’t imagine a fairy wearing boots, could you? Especially with copper toes? We are going to decorate the hall with creeping spruce and fir mottoes with pink tissue-paper roses in them. And we are all to march in two by two after the audience is seated, while Emma White plays a march on the organ. Oh, Marilla, I know you are not so enthusiastic about it as I am, but don’t you hope your little Anne will distinguish herself?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，当你能把爱国主义和乐趣结合起来时，不是吗？当然，能举办一场音乐会真是太好了。我们将有六个合唱团，戴安娜将独唱。我有两个对话——‘制止流言协会’和‘仙女女王’。男孩们也将有一个对话。我要朗诵两场，玛丽拉。一想到这些我就发抖。是的，但最后我们会看到一个画面——“信仰、希望和慈善”。我和戴安娜、鲁比都穿着白色的衣服，头发飘逸，我要双手紧握，抬起眼睛，如果你听到我的声音，请不要惊慌。我不得不在其中发出令人心碎的呻吟，而玛丽拉却很闷闷不乐，因为她想成为仙女女王，这太荒谬了，因为谁听说过像乔西这样胖的仙女女王一定是苗条的，而我就是其中之一。伴娘们说，她认为红头发的仙女和胖仙女一样可笑，但我不介意乔西说我要在头发上戴一顶白玫瑰花环，而鲁比·吉利斯会把她的拖鞋借给我，因为我自己没有拖鞋，你知道，你无法想象仙女穿着靴子，尤其是铜脚趾的吗？用匍匐的云杉和冷杉格言装饰大厅，观众入座后，我们都要两两行进，而艾玛·怀特则用管风琴演奏进行曲，哦，玛丽拉，我知道你不像我那么热衷，但你不希望你的小安妮能脱颖而出吗？

chapters.title: Chapter 25: Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 25 章：马修送安妮泡泡袖礼服

paragraphs.en: MATTHEW was having a bad ten minutes of it. He had come into the kitchen, in the twilight of a cold, gray December evening, and had sat down in the woodbox corner to take off his heavy boots, unconscious of the fact that Anne and a bevy of her schoolmates were having a practice of “The Fairy Queen” in the sitting room. Presently they came trooping through the hall and out into the kitchen, laughing and chattering gaily. They did not see Matthew, who shrank bashfully back into the shadows beyond the woodbox with a boot in one hand and a bootjack in the other, and he watched them shyly for the aforesaid ten minutes as they put on caps and jackets and talked about the dialogue and the concert. Anne stood among them, bright eyed and animated as they; but Matthew suddenly became conscious that there was something about her different from her mates. And what worried Matthew was that the difference impressed him as being something that should not exist. Anne had a brighter face, and bigger, starrier eyes, and more delicate features than the other; even shy, unobservant Matthew had learned to take note of these things; but the difference that disturbed him did not consist in any of these respects. Then in what did it consist?
paragraphs.zh: 马修经历了很糟糕的十分钟。他在十二月一个寒冷、灰暗的夜晚的暮色中走进厨房，坐在木箱角落里脱掉沉重的靴子，没有意识到安妮和她的一群同学正在客厅里练习《仙女女王》。不久，他们成群结队地穿过大厅，走进厨房，欢快地笑着、闲聊着。他们没有看到马修，他一手拿着靴子，另一只手拿着脱鞋器，害羞地缩回木箱外面的阴影里，他害羞地看着他们在上述十分钟里戴上帽子和夹克，谈论对话和音乐会。安妮站在他们中间，和他们一样眼睛明亮，充满活力。但马修突然意识到她和她的伙伴们有些不同。让马修担心的是，这种差异给他留下的印象是不应该存在的。安妮的脸比其他人更明亮，眼睛更大，更有星星，五官也更精致。即使是害羞、不善于观察的马修也学会了注意这些事情。但令他不安的差异并不在于这些方面。那么它的内容是什么？

paragraphs.en: “Oh, certainly--certainly--just as you say,” stammered unhappy Matthew, seizing the rake and making for the door. At the threshold he recollected that he had not paid for it and he turned miserably back. While Miss Harris was counting out his change he rallied his powers for a final desperate attempt. “Well now--if it isn’t too much trouble--I might as well--that is--I’d like to look at--at--some sugar.” “There’s a barrel of it over there,” said Miss Harris, shaking her bangles at it. “It’s the only kind we have.” “I’ll--I’ll take twenty pounds of it,” said Matthew, with beads of perspiration standing on his forehead.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，当然——当然——正如你所说，”马修不高兴地结结巴巴地说，抓起耙子向门口走去。到了门口，他才想起自己还没有付钱，便痛苦地转身回去。当哈里斯小姐正在数着他的改变时，他集结力量进行了最后的绝望尝试。 “那么现在——如果不是太麻烦的话——我不妨——也就是说——我想看看——一些糖。” “那边有一桶，”哈里斯小姐一边说，一边对着它晃动手镯。 “这是我们唯一拥有的一种。” “我要——我要二十磅，”马修说，额头上冒出了汗珠。

paragraphs.en: “Merry Christmas, Marilla! Merry Christmas, Matthew! Isn’t it a lovely Christmas? I’m so glad it’s white. Any other kind of Christmas doesn’t seem real, does it? I don’t like green Christmases. They’re not green--they’re just nasty faded browns and grays. What makes people call them green? Why--why--Matthew, is that for me? Oh, Matthew!” Matthew had sheepishly unfolded the dress from its paper swathings and held it out with a deprecatory glance at Marilla, who feigned to be contemptuously filling the teapot, but nevertheless watched the scene out of the corner of her eye with a rather interested air.
paragraphs.zh: “圣诞快乐，玛丽拉！圣诞快乐，马修！这不是一个可爱的圣诞节吗？我很高兴它是白色的。任何其他形式的圣诞节看起来都不真实，不是吗？我不喜欢绿色的圣诞节。它们不是绿色的——它们只是令人讨厌的褪色的棕色和灰色。是什么让人们称它们为绿色？为什么——为什么——马修，这是给我的吗？哦，马修！”马修羞涩地把裙子从纸巾里展开，递过来，鄙视地看了玛丽拉一眼，玛丽拉假装轻蔑地往茶壶里倒茶，但仍然用眼角余光饶有兴趣地看着这一幕。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, hasn’t it been a brilliant evening?” sighed Anne, when it was all over and she and Diana were walking home together under a dark, starry sky. “Everything went off very well,” said Diana practically. “I guess we must have made as much as ten dollars. Mind you, Mr. Allan is going to send an account of it to the Charlottetown papers.” “Oh, Diana, will we really see our names in print? It makes me thrill to think of it. Your solo was perfectly elegant, Diana. I felt prouder than you did when it was encored. I just said to myself, ‘It is my dear bosom friend who is so honored.’”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，这不是一个美好的夜晚吗？”安妮叹了口气，一切都结束了，她和戴安娜在黑暗的星空下一起走回家。 “一切都很顺利，”戴安娜实际说道。 “我想我们肯定赚了十美元。请注意，艾伦先生将把此事发给夏洛特敦的报纸。” “哦，戴安娜，我们真的会看到我们的名字出现在印刷品上吗？一想到这一点就让我激动不已。戴安娜，你的独奏非常优雅。当它被重新演唱时，我感到比你更自豪。我只是对自己说，‘这是我亲爱的知音，我感到非常荣幸。’”

chapters.title: Chapter 26: The Story Club is Formed
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 26 章：故事俱乐部与创作热情

paragraphs.en: JUNIOR Avonlea found it hard to settle down to humdrum existence again. To Anne in particular things seemed fearfully flat, stale, and unprofitable after the goblet of excitement she had been sipping for weeks. Could she go back to the former quiet pleasures of those faraway days before the concert? At first, as she told Diana, she did not really think she could.
paragraphs.zh: 小埃文利发现很难再次安定下来过单调的生活。尤其是对安妮来说，在她喝了几个星期的兴奋之杯之后，一切似乎都极其平淡、陈旧、无利可图。她还能回到演唱会前那段遥远的日子里的安静快乐吗？起初，正如她告诉戴安娜的那样，她真的认为自己做不到。

paragraphs.en: “Ruby Gillis thinks of nothing but beaus,” said Anne disdainfully. “She’s actually delighted when anyone writes her name up in a take-notice for all she pretends to be so mad. But I’m afraid that is an uncharitable speech. Mrs. Allan says we should never make uncharitable speeches; but they do slip out so often before you think, don’t they? I simply can’t talk about Josie Pye without making an uncharitable speech, so I never mention her at all. You may have noticed that. I’m trying to be as much like Mrs. Allan as I possibly can, for I think she’s perfect. Mr. Allan thinks so too. Mrs. Lynde says he just worships the ground she treads on and she doesn’t really think it right for a minister to set his affections so much on a mortal being. But then, Diana, even ministers are human and have their besetting sins just like everybody else. I had such an interesting talk with Mrs. Allan about besetting sins last Sunday afternoon. There are just a few things it’s proper to talk about on Sundays and that is one of them. My besetting sin is imagining too much and forgetting my duties. I’m striving very hard to overcome it and now that I’m really thirteen perhaps I’ll get on better.”
paragraphs.zh: “鲁比·吉利斯只想着情人。”安妮轻蔑地说。 “当有人把她的名字写在记事本上时，她真的很高兴，因为她假装很生气。但我担心这是一次无情的演讲。艾伦夫人说我们永远不应该发表无情的演讲；但它们确实经常在你想到之前就溜走，不是吗？我根本无法在不做无情的演讲的情况下谈论乔西·派伊，所以我从来没有提到过她。你可能已经注意到了。我正在努力做到这一点。我尽可能地像艾伦夫人一样，因为我认为艾伦先生也这么认为，林德夫人说他只是崇拜她所踏过的土地，她认为牧师将自己的感情如此之多地放在凡人身上是不正确的，但戴安娜，即使是牧师也像其他人一样有他们困扰的罪孽。这些只是周日应该谈论的几件事，其中之一就是我的想象太多，忘记了我的职责，我正在努力克服它，现在我真的十三岁了，也许我会过得更好。”

paragraphs.en: “I wrote it last Monday evening. It’s called ‘The Jealous Rival; or In Death Not Divided.’ I read it to Marilla and she said it was stuff and nonsense. Then I read it to Matthew and he said it was fine. That is the kind of critic I like. It’s a sad, sweet story. I just cried like a child while I was writing it. It’s about two beautiful maidens called Cordelia Montmorency and Geraldine Seymour who lived in the same village and were devotedly attached to each other. Cordelia was a regal brunette with a coronet of midnight hair and duskly flashing eyes. Geraldine was a queenly blonde with hair like spun gold and velvety purple eyes.”
paragraphs.zh: “我上周一晚上写的。它的名字叫《嫉妒的对手；或者死亡不分》。我读给玛丽拉听，她说这是胡说八道。然后我读给马修听，他说这很好。我喜欢那种评论家。这是一个悲伤而甜蜜的故事。我写的时候哭得像个孩子。这是关于两个美丽的少女，名叫科迪莉亚·蒙莫朗西和杰拉尔丁·西摩，她们住在美国科迪莉亚是一位高贵的黑发女郎，有着一顶午夜般的头发和一双闪烁着光芒的昏暗的眼睛，她是一位女王般的金发女郎，有着金色的头发和天鹅绒般的紫色眼睛。

paragraphs.en: “It’s extremely interesting,” Anne told Marilla. “Each girl has to read her story out loud and then we talk it over. We are going to keep them all sacredly and have them to read to our descendants. We each write under a nom-de-plume. Mine is Rosamond Montmorency. All the girls do pretty well. Ruby Gillis is rather sentimental. She puts too much lovemaking into her stories and you know too much is worse than too little. Jane never puts any because she says it makes her feel so silly when she had to read it out loud. Jane’s stories are extremely sensible. Then Diana puts too many murders into hers. She says most of the time she doesn’t know what to do with the people so she kills them off to get rid of them. I mostly always have to tell them what to write about, but that isn’t hard for I’ve millions of ideas.”
paragraphs.zh: “这非常有趣，”安妮告诉玛丽拉。 “每个女孩都必须大声朗读她的故事，然后我们再讨论。我们将把它们都神圣地保存下来，并让它们读给我们的后代听。我们每个人都用化名写作。我的名字是罗莎蒙德·蒙莫朗西。所有女孩都做得很好。鲁比·吉利斯相当多愁善感。她在她的故事中加入了太多的爱，你知道太多比太少更糟糕。简从来不放任何东西，因为她说当她不得不读出来时，这让她觉得很傻简的故事非常明智，然后戴安娜在她的故事中加入了太多的谋杀，她说大多数时候她不知道如何处理这些人，所以她总是要告诉他们要写什么，但这并不难。”

chapters.title: Chapter 27: Vanity and Vexation of Spirit
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 27 章：买绿染料染发变绿风波

paragraphs.en: MARILLA, walking home one late April evening from an Aid meeting, realized that the winter was over and gone with the thrill of delight that spring never fails to bring to the oldest and saddest as well as to the youngest and merriest. Marilla was not given to subjective analysis of her thoughts and feelings. She probably imagined that she was thinking about the Aids and their missionary box and the new carpet for the vestry room, but under these reflections was a harmonious consciousness of red fields smoking into pale-purply mists in the declining sun, of long, sharp-pointed fir shadows falling over the meadow beyond the brook, of still, crimson-budded maples around a mirrorlike wood pool, of a wakening in the world and a stir of hidden pulses under the gray sod. The spring was abroad in the land and Marilla’s sober, middle-aged step was lighter and swifter because of its deep, primal gladness.
paragraphs.zh: 四月下旬的一个晚上，玛丽拉从一次援助会议走回家时，意识到冬天已经过去了，春天总是给最年长、最悲伤的人和最年轻、最快乐的人带来喜悦的兴奋。马里拉不喜欢对自己的想法和感受进行主观分析。她可能想象自己正在思考艾滋、他们的传教士箱和礼拜室的新地毯，但在这些反射下，是一种和谐的意识：红色的田野在夕阳下冒着烟，化为淡紫色的薄雾，长长的、尖锐的冷杉树影落在小溪对面的草地上，静谧的、在镜子般的木池周围发芽的深红色枫树，世界的苏醒和灰色草皮下隐藏的脉动的骚动。大地春意盎然，马瑞拉中年人清醒的脚步变得更轻、更快，因为它充满了深沉的、原始的快乐。

paragraphs.en: “No. But please, Marilla, go away and don’t look at me. I’m in the depths of despair and I don’t care who gets head in class or writes the best composition or sings in the Sunday-school choir any more. Little things like that are of no importance now because I don’t suppose I’ll ever be able to go anywhere again. My career is closed. Please, Marilla, go away and don’t look at me.” “Did anyone ever hear the like?” the mystified Marilla wanted to know. “Anne Shirley, whatever is the matter with you? What have you done? Get right up this minute and tell me. This minute, I say. There now, what is it?”
paragraphs.zh: “不。但是，玛丽拉，请走开，别看我。我正处于绝望的深渊，我不在乎谁在课堂上领先，谁写出最好的作文，或者谁在主日学校唱诗班唱歌。这样的小事现在都不重要了，因为我想我再也不能去任何地方了。我的职业生涯已经结束了。求求你，玛丽拉，走开，别看我。” “有人听过类似的话吗？”困惑的玛丽拉想知道。 “安妮·雪莉，你怎么了？你做了什么？马上站起来告诉我。我说，现在就告诉我。现在，怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: “Well,” said Marilla sarcastically, “if I’d decided it was worth while to dye my hair I’d have dyed it a decent color at least. I wouldn’t have dyed it green.” “But I didn’t mean to dye it green, Marilla,” protested Anne dejectedly. “If I was wicked I meant to be wicked to some purpose. He said it would turn my hair a beautiful raven black--he positively assured me that it would. How could I doubt his word, Marilla? I know what it feels like to have your word doubted. And Mrs. Allan says we should never suspect anyone of not telling us the truth unless we have proof that they’re not. I have proof now--green hair is proof enough for anybody. But I hadn’t then and I believed every word he said implicitly.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”玛丽拉讽刺地说，“如果我认为值得染头发，我至少会染成像样的颜色。我不会把它染成绿色。” “但我不是故意把它染成绿色的，玛丽拉，”安妮沮丧地抗议道。 “如果我是邪恶的，我就意味着为了某种目的而邪恶。他说这会让我的头发变成美丽的乌鸦黑——他肯定地向我保证它会的。我怎么能怀疑他的诺言，玛丽拉？我知道你的诺言受到怀疑是什么感觉。艾伦太太说，我们永远不应该怀疑任何人没有告诉我们真相，除非我们有证据证明他们没有告诉我们真相。我现在有证据——绿色的头发对任何人来说都足以证明。但我当时没有，我相信每一个。他含蓄地说了一句话。”

paragraphs.en: Anne’s lips quivered, but she realized the bitter truth of Marilla’s remarks. With a dismal sigh she went for the scissors. “Please cut it off at once, Marilla, and have it over. Oh, I feel that my heart is broken. This is such an unromantic affliction. The girls in books lose their hair in fevers or sell it to get money for some good deed, and I’m sure I wouldn’t mind losing my hair in some such fashion half so much. But there is nothing comforting in having your hair cut off because you’ve dyed it a dreadful color, is there? I’m going to weep all the time you’re cutting it off, if it won’t interfere. It seems such a tragic thing.”
paragraphs.zh: 安妮的嘴唇颤抖着，但她意识到玛丽拉话里的苦涩事实。她沮丧地叹了口气，去拿剪刀。 “请立刻把它剪掉，玛丽拉，结束吧。哦，我感觉我的心都碎了。这真是一种不浪漫的痛苦。书里的女孩们会因为发烧而掉头发，或者卖掉头发来换取一些善行的钱，我相信我不会介意以这种方式失去一半的头发。但是，因为你把头发染成了可怕的颜色，所以把头发剪掉了，这并没有什么安慰，不是吗？我要去如果它不干扰的话，你就一直哭泣，这似乎是一件悲惨的事情。”

chapters.title: Chapter 28: An Unfortunate Lily Maid
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 28 章：扮演“百合少女”小船沉没救援

paragraphs.en: OF course you must be Elaine, Anne,” said Diana. “I could never have the courage to float down there.” “Nor I,” said Ruby Gillis, with a shiver. “I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead--I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright.” “Of course it would be romantic,” conceded Jane Andrews, “but I know I couldn’t keep still. I’d be popping up every minute or so to see where I was and if I wasn’t drifting too far out. And you know, Anne, that would spoil the effect.”
paragraphs.zh: 当然，你一定是伊莱恩，安妮，”戴安娜说。“我永远没有勇气飘到那里去。 “我也一样，”鲁比·吉利斯颤抖着说道。 “当我们有两三个人在公寓里并且我们可以坐起来时，我不介意漂浮下来。那很有趣。但躺下来假装我已经死了——我就是做不到。我真的会被吓死的。” “这当然很浪漫，”简·安德鲁斯承认，“但我知道我不能保持静止。我大约每隔一分钟就会出现一次，看看我在哪里，看看我是否偏离得太远。你知道，安妮，这会破坏效果。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’ll be Elaine,” said Anne, yielding reluctantly, for, although she would have been delighted to play the principal character, yet her artistic sense demanded fitness for it and this, she felt, her limitations made impossible. “Ruby, you must be King Arthur and Jane will be Guinevere and Diana must be Lancelot. But first you must be the brothers and the father. We can’t have the old dumb servitor because there isn’t room for two in the flat when one is lying down. We must pall the barge all its length in blackest samite. That old black shawl of your mother’s will be just the thing, Diana.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我会扮演伊莱恩，”安妮不情愿地屈服了，因为虽然她很乐意扮演主角，但她的艺术感要求适合它，而她觉得，她的局限性使得这一点变得不可能。 “鲁比，你必须是亚瑟王，简将是格尼薇儿，戴安娜必须是兰斯洛特。但首先你必须是兄弟和父亲。我们不能有那个又老又笨的仆人，因为当一个人躺下时，公寓里没有足够的空间容纳两个人。我们必须用最黑的锦缎铺满驳船。你母亲的那条旧黑围巾正适合你，戴安娜。”

paragraphs.en: The minutes passed by, each seeming an hour to the unfortunate lily maid. Why didn’t somebody come? Where had the girls gone? Suppose they had fainted, one and all! Suppose nobody ever came! Suppose she grew so tired and cramped that she could hold on no longer! Anne looked at the wicked green depths below her, wavering with long, oily shadows, and shivered. Her imagination began to suggest all manner of gruesome possibilities to her. Then, just as she thought she really could not endure the ache in her arms and wrists another moment, Gilbert Blythe came rowing under the bridge in Harmon Andrews’s dory!
paragraphs.zh: 时间一分一秒过去，对于不幸的百合女仆来说，每一分钟都像是一个小时。为什么没有人来？女孩们去哪儿了？假设他们都晕倒了！假设没有人来！假设她累得筋疲力尽，再也坚持不住了！安妮看着下面邪恶的绿色深处，长长的、油腻的阴影在摇曳，她颤抖着。她的想象力开始向她暗示各种可怕的可能性。然后，正当她以为自己真的再也无法忍受手臂和手腕的疼痛时，吉尔伯特·布莱斯驾着哈蒙·安德鲁斯的平底小平底船划到了桥下！

paragraphs.en: He pulled away with swift defiant strokes, and Anne went up the steep, ferny little path under the maples. She held her head very high, but she was conscious of an odd feeling of regret. She almost wished she had answered Gilbert differently. Of course, he had insulted her terribly, but still--! Altogether, Anne rather thought it would be a relief to sit down and have a good cry. She was really quite unstrung, for the reaction from her fright and cramped clinging was making itself felt.
paragraphs.zh: 他快速、挑衅地把车开开，安妮走上枫树下那条陡峭、长满蕨类植物的小路。她把头昂得很高，但心里却有一种奇怪的遗憾。她几乎希望自己能以不同的方式回答吉尔伯特。当然，他已经严重侮辱了她，但是——！总而言之，安妮觉得坐下来好好哭一场会是一种解脱。她真的很紧张，因为她的恐惧和局促的依恋所带来的反应已经显而易见。

chapters.title: Chapter 29: An Epoch in Anne's Life
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 29 章：拜访夏洛特敦与城市见闻

paragraphs.en: ANNE was bringing the cows home from the back pasture by way of Lover’s Lane. It was a September evening and all the gaps and clearings in the woods were brimmed up with ruby sunset light. Here and there the lane was splashed with it, but for the most part it was already quite shadowy beneath the maples, and the spaces under the firs were filled with a clear violet dusk like airy wine. The winds were out in their tops, and there is no sweeter music on earth than that which the wind makes in the fir trees at evening.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮正从情人巷把奶牛从后面的牧场带回家。那是九月的一个傍晚，树林里的所有缝隙和空地都被红宝石色的夕阳照亮。巷子里到处都洒满了它，但大部分地方在枫树下已经很阴暗了，冷杉下的空间充满了清澈的紫罗兰色黄昏，就像空气中的酒一样。风从山顶吹来，世界上没有比傍晚的风吹过冷杉树更悦耳的音乐了。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Diana,” whispered Anne, finding it necessary to lean up against a maple tree for support, “do you really mean it? But I’m afraid Marilla won’t let me go. She will say that she can’t encourage gadding about. That was what she said last week when Jane invited me to go with them in their double-seated buggy to the American concert at the White Sands Hotel. I wanted to go, but Marilla said I’d be better at home learning my lessons and so would Jane. I was bitterly disappointed, Diana. I felt so heartbroken that I wouldn’t say my prayers when I went to bed. But I repented of that and got up in the middle of the night and said them.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，戴安娜，”安妮发现有必要靠在枫树上支撑，低声说道，“你真的是这个意思吗？但是我担心玛丽拉不会让我走。她会说她不能鼓励我到处闲逛。上周简邀请我和他们一起乘坐双人马车去白沙酒店参加美国音乐会时，她就是这么说的。我想去，但玛丽拉说我最好在家学习功课，所以简，我非常失望，我感到非常伤心，所以我在睡觉时没有祈祷，但我后悔了，并在半夜起床说了这些祈祷。”

paragraphs.en: “Velvet carpet,” sighed Anne luxuriously, “and silk curtains! I’ve dreamed of such things, Diana. But do you know I don’t believe I feel very comfortable with them after all. There are so many things in this room and all so splendid that there is no scope for imagination. That is one consolation when you are poor--there are so many more things you can imagine about.” Their sojourn in town was something that Anne and Diana dated from for years. From first to last it was crowded with delights. On Wednesday Miss Barry took them to the Exhibition grounds and kept them there all day.
paragraphs.zh: “天鹅绒地毯，”安妮奢华地叹了口气，“还有丝绸窗帘！我梦想过这样的东西，戴安娜。但是你知道吗，我不相信我对它们感到很舒服。这间屋子里的东西太多了，而且都那么华丽，没有想象的余地。这是你贫穷时的一种安慰——你可以想象的东西还有很多。”安妮和戴安娜在城里的逗留已经约会了很多年。自始至终，这里都充满了欢乐。周三，巴里小姐带他们去了展览场地，并让他们在那里呆了一整天。

paragraphs.en: “I’ve enjoyed every minute of the time,” said Anne, throwing her arms impulsively about the old woman’s neck and kissing her wrinkled cheek. Diana would never have dared to do such a thing and felt rather aghast at Anne’s freedom. But Miss Barry was pleased, and she stood on her veranda and watched the buggy out of sight. Then she went back into her big house with a sigh. It seemed very lonely, lacking those fresh young lives. Miss Barry was a rather selfish old lady, if the truth must be told, and had never cared much for anybody but herself. She valued people only as they were of service to her or amused her. Anne had amused her, and consequently stood high in the old lady’s good graces. But Miss Barry found herself thinking less about Anne’s quaint speeches than of her fresh enthusiasms, her transparent emotions, her little winning ways, and the sweetness of her eyes and lips.
paragraphs.zh: “我很享受这段时间的每一分钟，”安妮说，她冲动地用双臂搂住老妇人的脖子，亲吻她布满皱纹的脸颊。戴安娜绝对不敢做这样的事，她对安妮的自由感到非常震惊。但巴里小姐很高兴，她站在阳台上，看着马车消失在视线之外。然后她叹了一口气，回到了自己的大房子里。显得很孤独，缺少了那些新鲜的年轻生命。说实话，巴里小姐是一位相当自私的老太太，除了她自己之外，从来不关心任何人。她只看重那些为她服务或让她开心的人。安妮逗乐了她，因此赢得了老太太的青睐。但巴里小姐发现自己想的不是安妮古怪的演讲，而是她新鲜的热情、她透明的情感、她小小的胜利之道，以及她眼睛和嘴唇的甜蜜。

chapters.title: Chapter 30: The Queen's Class is Formed
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 30 章：葵因学院考前准备班成立

paragraphs.en: MARILLA laid her knitting on her lap and leaned back in her chair. Her eyes were tired, and she thought vaguely that she must see about having her glasses changed the next time she went to town, for her eyes had grown tired very often of late. It was nearly dark, for the full November twilight had fallen around Green Gables, and the only light in the kitchen came from the dancing red flames in the stove.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉把编织的东西放在腿上，靠在椅子上。她的眼睛很累，她隐隐约约地想，下次进城时一定要注意换一下眼镜，因为最近她的眼睛经常感到疲劳。天几乎黑了，因为整个十一月的暮色已经笼罩在绿山墙周围，厨房里唯一的光来自炉子里舞动的红色火焰。

paragraphs.en: “Well, I guess I’ll light the lamp and get to work,” said Marilla. “I see plainly that you don’t want to hear what Miss Stacy had to say. You’re more interested in the sound of your own tongue than in anything else.” “Oh, indeed, Marilla, I do want to hear it,” cried Anne contritely. “I won’t say another word--not one. I know I talk too much, but I am really trying to overcome it, and although I say far too much, yet if you only knew how many things I want to say and don’t, you’d give me some credit for it. Please tell me, Marilla.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我想我会点灯开始工作，”马里拉说。 “我看得很清楚，你不想听史黛西小姐说的话。你对自己的舌头声音比对其他任何事情都更感兴趣。” “哦，确实如此，玛丽拉，我确实想听听。”安妮悔恨地喊道。 “我不会再说一个字——一个也不会。我知道我说得太多了，但我真的在努力克服它，虽然我说得太多了，但如果你知道我想说和不想说的事情有多少，你就会给我一些信任。请告诉我，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t happen to know what Gilbert Blythe’s ambition in life is--if he has any,” said Anne scornfully. There was open rivalry between Gilbert and Anne now. Previously the rivalry had been rather one-sided, but there was no longer any doubt that Gilbert was as determined to be first in class as Anne was. He was a foeman worthy of her steel. The other members of the class tacitly acknowledged their superiority, and never dreamed of trying to compete with them.
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道吉尔伯特·布莱斯的人生抱负是什么——如果他有的话，”安妮轻蔑地说。吉尔伯特和安妮之间现在存在着公开的竞争。之前的竞争相当一边倒，但毫无疑问，吉尔伯特和安妮一样决心要获得班上第一。他是一个值得她钢铁般对待的敌人。班里的其他同学都默认了他们的优势，从来没有想过要与他们竞争。

paragraphs.en: “Hurrah!” said Moody Spurgeon. Moody Spurgeon had never been so carried away by his feelings before, and he blushed uncomfortably every time he thought about it for a week. “Oh, I’m so glad,” said Anne, with shining eyes. “Dear Stacy, it would be perfectly dreadful if you didn’t come back. I don’t believe I could have the heart to go on with my studies at all if another teacher came here.” When Anne got home that night she stacked all her textbooks away in an old trunk in the attic, locked it, and threw the key into the blanket box.
paragraphs.zh: “欢呼！”穆迪·司布真说。穆迪·司布真从来没有这么被自己的感情冲昏过头脑，一周以来，每次想到这件事，他都会脸红得不自在。 “哦，我太高兴了，”安妮眼睛闪闪发亮地说。 “亲爱的史黛西，如果你不回来，那将是非常可怕的。我不相信如果有另一个老师来到这里，我根本没有勇气继续我的学习。”那天晚上，安妮回到家后，她把所有的课本都堆放在阁楼的一个旧箱子里，锁上，然后把钥匙扔进毯子箱里。

chapters.title: Chapter 31: Where the Brook and River Meet
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 31 章：少年与青春的转折点

paragraphs.en: ANNE had her “good” summer and enjoyed it wholeheartedly. She and Diana fairly lived outdoors, reveling in all the delights that Lover’s Lane and the Dryad’s Bubble and Willowmere and Victoria Island afforded. Marilla offered no objections to Anne’s gypsyings. The Spencervale doctor who had come the night Minnie May had the croup met Anne at the house of a patient one afternoon early in vacation, looked her over sharply, screwed up his mouth, shook his head, and sent a message to Marilla Cuthbert by another person. It was: “Keep that redheaded girl of yours in the open air all summer and don’t let her read books until she gets more spring into her step.”
paragraphs.zh: 安妮度过了她“美好”的夏天，并且全心全意地享受着它。她和戴安娜几乎都生活在户外，陶醉在情人巷、树精泡泡、威洛米尔和维多利亚岛所提供的所有乐趣中。玛丽拉对安妮的吉普赛生活没有提出异议。米妮·梅患哮吼的那天晚上，斯宾塞维尔的医生在假期的一个下午早些时候在一位病人家里见到了安妮，他严厉地打量了她一眼，抿紧了嘴，摇了摇头，然后由另一个人给玛丽拉·库斯伯特发了一条信息。它是：“让你的那个红发女孩整个夏天都待在户外，不要让她读书，直到她的步伐更加灵活。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m very glad you feel the same,” said Anne decidedly. “It’s so encouraging. I shan’t worry so much over that after this. But I dare say there’ll be other things to worry me. They keep coming up new all the time--things to perplex you, you know. You settle one question and there’s another right after. There are so many things to be thought over and decided when you’re beginning to grow up. It keeps me busy all the time thinking them over and deciding what is right. It’s a serious thing to grow up, isn’t it, Marilla? But when I have such good friends as you and Matthew and Mrs. Allan and Miss Stacy I ought to grow up successfully, and I’m sure it will be my own fault if I don’t. I feel it’s a great responsibility because I have only the one chance. If I don’t grow up right I can’t go back and begin over again. I’ve grown two inches this summer, Marilla. Mr. Gillis measured me at Ruby’s party. I’m so glad you made my new dresses longer. That dark-green one is so pretty and it was sweet of you to put on the flounce. Of course I know it wasn’t really necessary, but flounces are so stylish this fall and Josie Pye has flounces on all her dresses. I know I’ll be able to study better because of mine. I shall have such a comfortable feeling deep down in my mind about that flounce.”
paragraphs.zh: “我很高兴你也有同样的感觉。”安妮斩钉截铁地说。 “这太令人鼓舞了。以后我不会再担心那么多了。但我敢说还会有其他事情让我担心。他们一直在不断出现新的事情——让你困惑的事情，你知道。你解决了一个问题，然后还有另一个问题。当你开始长大时，有很多事情需要考虑和决定。这让我一直忙于思考它们并决定什么是正确的。成长是一件严肃的事情，不是吗？玛丽拉？但是当我有你、马修、艾伦夫人和史黛西小姐这样的好朋友时，我确信如果我没有成长，那将是我自己的错，因为我只有一次机会，今年夏天我就不能再重新开始了，玛丽拉先生在鲁比的聚会上测量了我的身高。我的那件深绿色的衣服真漂亮，你穿荷叶边真是太好了，我当然知道这不是真的必要，但荷叶边今年秋天很时尚，乔西·派伊（Josie Pye）的所有衣服上都有荷叶边，我知道我会因为我的荷叶边而有一种舒服的感觉。”

paragraphs.en: “I was thinking about Anne,” she explained. “She’s got to be such a big girl--and she’ll probably be away from us next winter. I’ll miss her terrible.” “She’ll be able to come home often,” comforted Matthew, to whom Anne was as yet and always would be the little, eager girl he had brought home from Bright River on that June evening four years before. “The branch railroad will be built to Carmody by that time.” “It won’t be the same thing as having her here all the time,” sighed Marilla gloomily, determined to enjoy her luxury of grief uncomforted. “But there--men can’t understand these things!”
paragraphs.zh: “我在想安妮，”她解释道。 “她一定是个大女孩了——明年冬天她可能就会离开我们。我会非常想念她的。” “她会经常回家的。”马修安慰道，对马修来说，安妮至今仍然是、永远是四年前那个六月的晚上他从布赖特河带回家的那个热切的小女孩。 “届时，通往卡莫迪的支线铁路将建成。” “这和她一直待在这里是不一样的。”玛丽拉阴沉地叹了口气，决心享受她不受安慰的悲伤的奢侈。 “但是——人类无法理解这些事情！”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know--I don’t want to talk as much,” she said, denting her chin thoughtfully with her forefinger. “It’s nicer to think dear, pretty thoughts and keep them in one’s heart, like treasures. I don’t like to have them laughed at or wondered over. And somehow I don’t want to use big words any more. It’s almost a pity, isn’t it, now that I’m really growing big enough to say them if I did want to. It’s fun to be almost grown up in some ways, but it’s not the kind of fun I expected, Marilla. There’s so much to learn and do and think that there isn’t time for big words. Besides, Miss Stacy says the short ones are much stronger and better. She makes us write all our essays as simply as possible. It was hard at first. I was so used to crowding in all the fine big words I could think of--and I thought of any number of them. But I’ve got used to it now and I see it’s so much better.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道——我不想说太多，”她说，用食指若有所思地压着下巴。 “亲爱的、美丽的想法，并把它们像珍宝一样放在心里，这样会更好。我不喜欢让它们被嘲笑或好奇。不知怎的，我不想再使用大词了。这几乎是一种遗憾，不是吗，现在我真的长大了，如果我愿意的话，可以说出来。在某些方面，几乎长大是很有趣的，但这不是我所期望的那种乐趣，玛丽拉。此外，史黛西小姐说，她让我们尽可能简单地写出所有的文章，我很难习惯把所有能想到的好词塞进去——但我现在已经习惯了，而且我发现它好多了。

chapters.title: Chapter 32: The Pass List is Out
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 32 章：放榜荣登葵因榜首

paragraphs.en: WITH the end of June came the close of the term and the close of Miss Stacy’s rule in Avonlea school. Anne and Diana walked home that evening feeling very sober indeed. Red eyes and damp handkerchiefs bore convincing testimony to the fact that Miss Stacy’s farewell words must have been quite as touching as Mr. Phillips’s had been under similar circumstances three years before. Diana looked back at the schoolhouse from the foot of the spruce hill and sighed deeply. “It does seem as if it was the end of everything, doesn’t it?” she said dismally. “You oughtn’t to feel half as badly as I do,” said Anne, hunting vainly for a dry spot on her handkerchief. “You’ll be back again next winter, but I suppose I’ve left the dear old school forever--if I have good luck, that is.”
paragraphs.zh: 六月底，学期结束了，史黛西小姐在埃文利学校的统治也结束了。那天晚上，安妮和戴安娜走回家，感觉确实非常清醒。红红的眼睛和湿漉漉的手帕令人信服地证明，史黛西小姐的告别词一定和三年前菲利普斯先生在类似情况下的告别词一样感人。黛安娜在云杉山脚下回望校舍，深深地叹了口气。 “看来一切都结束了，不是吗？”她沮丧地说。 “你的感觉不应该像我一样糟糕。”安妮一边说，一边徒劳地在手帕上寻找一块干燥的地方。 “明年冬天你会再次回来，但我想我已经永远离开了亲爱的老学校——如果我运气好的话。”

paragraphs.en: “Here it is Tuesday night and I’m writing this in the library at Beechwood. Last night I was horribly lonesome all alone in my room and wished so much you were with me. I couldn’t ‘cram’ because I’d promised Miss Stacy not to, but it was as hard to keep from opening my history as it used to be to keep from reading a story before my lessons were learned.
paragraphs.zh: “现在是星期二晚上，我正在比奇伍德的图书馆里写这篇文章。昨晚，我一个人待在房间里，感到非常孤独，非常希望你能和我在一起。我不能‘临时抱佛脚’，因为我答应过史黛西小姐不要这么做，但我很难不去翻开我的历史，就像过去在我吸取教训之前不去读故事一样。

paragraphs.en: “Pretty well, I think, in everything but the geometry. I don’t know whether I passed in it or not and I have a creepy, crawly presentiment that I didn’t. Oh, how good it is to be back! Green Gables is the dearest, loveliest spot in the world.” “The girls say they know they didn’t pass, but I think they did pretty well. Josie says the geometry was so easy a child of ten could do it! Moody Spurgeon still thinks he failed in history and Charlie says he failed in algebra. But we don’t really know anything about it and won’t until the pass list is out. That won’t be for a fortnight. Fancy living a fortnight in such suspense! I wish I could go to sleep and never wake up until it is over.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想，除了几何之外，其他方面都很好。我不知道自己是否通过了，但我有一种令人毛骨悚然的预感，我没有通过。哦，回来真是太好了！绿山墙是世界上最可爱、最可爱的地方。” “女孩们说她们知道自己没有通过，但我认为她们考得很好。乔西说几何学太简单了，十岁的孩子就能做到！穆迪·斯布金仍然认为自己在历史上不及格，查理说他在代数上不及格。但我们对此一无所知，直到通过名单出来才知道。那不会是两周的时间。想象一下在这样的悬念中生活两周吧！我希望我能睡着，直到考试结束为止永远不会醒来。结束了。”

paragraphs.en: “Anne, you’ve passed,” she cried, “passed the very first--you and Gilbert both--you’re ties--but your name is first. Oh, I’m so proud!” Diana flung the paper on the table and herself on Anne’s bed, utterly breathless and incapable of further speech. Anne lighted the lamp, oversetting the match safe and using up half a dozen matches before her shaking hands could accomplish the task. Then she snatched up the paper. Yes, she had passed--there was her name at the very top of a list of two hundred! That moment was worth living for.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你通过了，”她喊道，“通过了第一名——你和吉尔伯特两人——你们是平手——但你的名字是第一名。哦，我太自豪了！”戴安娜把报纸扔在桌子上，把自己扔到安妮的床上，气喘吁吁，无法再说话。安妮点燃了灯，打翻了火柴保险柜，在她颤抖的双手完成任务之前，她已经用完了六根火柴。然后她一把抓起那张纸。是的，她已经通过了——她的名字排在两百个名单的最前面！那一刻值得为之而活。

chapters.title: Chapter 33: The Hotel Concert
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 33 章：白沙大饭店的惊艳朗诵

paragraphs.en: PUT on your white organdy, by all means, Anne,” advised Diana decidedly. They were together in the east gable chamber; outside it was only twilight--a lovely yellowish-green twilight with a clear-blue cloudless sky. A big round moon, slowly deepening from her pallid luster into burnished silver, hung over the Haunted Wood; the air was full of sweet summer sounds--sleepy birds twittering, freakish breezes, faraway voices and laughter. But in Anne’s room the blind was drawn and the lamp lighted, for an important toilet was being made.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜决然建议道：“一定要穿上你的白色纱裙，安妮。”他们一起在东山墙的房间里；外面只是暮色——可爱的黄绿色暮光，晴朗的蓝色万里无云的天空。一轮大圆月，从苍白的光泽慢慢加深成闪亮的银色，挂在闹鬼的树林上空；空气中充满了甜美的夏日声音——昏昏欲睡的鸟儿叽叽喳喳，怪异的微风，遥远的声音和但安妮的房间拉上了百叶窗，灯也亮着，因为正在建造一个重要的厕所。

paragraphs.en: “Shall I put my pearl beads on?” asked Anne. “Matthew brought me a string from town last week, and I know he’d like to see them on me.” Diana pursed up her lips, put her black head on one side critically, and finally pronounced in favor of the beads, which were thereupon tied around Anne’s slim milk-white throat. “There’s something so stylish about you, Anne,” said Diana, with unenvious admiration. “You hold your head with such an air. I suppose it’s your figure. I am just a dumpling. I’ve always been afraid of it, and now I know it is so. Well, I suppose I shall just have to resign myself to it.”
paragraphs.zh: “我可以戴上我的珍珠珠吗？”安妮问。 “马修上周从城里给我带来了一根绳子，我知道他希望在我身上看到它们。”戴安娜抿起嘴唇，挑剔地将黑头偏向一侧，最后宣布赞成珠子，珠子随即系在安妮纤细的乳白色喉咙上。 “安妮，你身上有一种很时尚的气质。”戴安娜带着毫不羡慕的钦佩说道。 “你昂着头的神情如此。我想这就是你的身材。我只是一个饺子。我一直很害怕它，现在我知道了。好吧，我想我只能听天由命了。”

paragraphs.en: “Don’t speak of your going away tonight,” begged Diana. “I don’t want to think of it, it makes me so miserable, and I do want to have a good time this evening. What are you going to recite, Anne? And are you nervous?” “Not a bit. I’ve recited so often in public I don’t mind at all now. I’ve decided to give ‘The Maiden’s Vow.’ It’s so pathetic. Laura Spencer is going to give a comic recitation, but I’d rather make people cry than laugh.” “They won’t dream of encoring me,” scoffed Anne, who was not without her own secret hopes that they would, and already visioned herself telling Matthew all about it at the next morning’s breakfast table. “There are Billy and Jane now--I hear the wheels. Come on.”
paragraphs.zh: “不要谈论你今晚要离开的事，”戴安娜恳求道。 “我不想去想它，它让我如此痛苦，而我今晚确实想玩得开心。安妮，你要背诵什么？你紧张吗？” “一点也不。我经常在公共场合朗诵，现在一点也不介意了。我决定念《少女的誓言》。这太可悲了。劳拉·斯宾塞要进行喜剧朗诵，但我宁愿让人哭也不愿让人笑。” “他们不会梦想让我加演的。”安妮嘲笑道，她自己也暗暗希望他们会加演，她已经想象自己会在第二天早上的早餐桌上把这一切告诉马修。 “现在比利和简来了——我听到了轮子的声音。来吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I can’t go,” said Anne confusedly. “But yet--I must, or Matthew will be disappointed. He said they would encore me.” Smiling, blushing, limpid eyed, Anne tripped back and gave a quaint, funny little selection that captivated her audience still further. The rest of the evening was quite a little triumph for her.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我不能去。”安妮困惑地说。 “但是——我必须这样做，否则马修会失望的。他说他们会给我加演。”安妮微笑着，脸红了，眼睛清澈，她回过头来，做了一个古怪、有趣的小选择，进一步吸引了她的观众。那天晚上剩下的时间对她来说是相当小的胜利。

chapters.title: Chapter 34: A Queen's Girl
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 34 章：告别绿山墙前往葵因学院

paragraphs.en: THE next three weeks were busy ones at Green Gables, for Anne was getting ready to go to Queen’s, and there was much sewing to be done, and many things to be talked over and arranged. Anne’s outfit was ample and pretty, for Matthew saw to that, and Marilla for once made no objections whatever to anything he purchased or suggested. More--one evening she went up to the east gable with her arms full of a delicate pale green material.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来的三周在绿山墙很忙碌，因为安妮正准备去皇后学院，还有很多缝纫工作要做，还有很多事情需要讨论和安排。安妮的衣服宽敞又漂亮，这是马修精心安排的，而玛丽拉这一次对他购买或建议的任何东西都没有提出异议。更重要的是，一天晚上，她怀里抱着一种精致的淡绿色材料，登上了东山墙。

paragraphs.en: “Marilla!” Anne sat down on Marilla’s gingham lap, took Marilla’s lined face between her hands, and looked gravely and tenderly into Marilla’s eyes. “I’m not a bit changed--not really. I’m only just pruned down and branched out. The real me--back here--is just the same. It won’t make a bit of difference where I go or how much I change outwardly; at heart I shall always be your little Anne, who will love you and Matthew and dear Green Gables more and better every day of her life.”
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉！”安妮坐在玛丽拉的格子腿上，双手捧着玛丽拉布满皱纹的脸，严肃而温柔地看着玛丽拉的眼睛。 “我没有一点改变——没有真正改变。我只是被修剪和扩展了。真正的我——回到这里——还是一样。我去哪里或我外表上有多大变化不会有一点区别；在内心深处，我将永远是你的小安妮，她会在生命中的每一天越来越爱你、马修和亲爱的绿山墙。”

paragraphs.en: It was lonesomer still when Anne found herself alone in her hall bedroom that night at twilight. She was not to board with the other girls, who all had relatives in town to take pity on them. Miss Josephine Barry would have liked to board her, but Beechwood was so far from the Academy that it was out of the question; so Miss Barry hunted up a boarding-house, assuring Matthew and Marilla that it was the very place for Anne. “The lady who keeps it is a reduced gentlewoman,” explained Miss Barry. “Her husband was a British officer, and she is very careful what sort of boarders she takes. Anne will not meet with any objectionable persons under her roof. The table is good, and the house is near the Academy, in a quiet neighborhood.”
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，黄昏时分，当安妮发现自己独自一人待在大厅的卧室里时，显得更加孤独。她不能和其他女孩一起寄宿，因为她们在城里都有亲戚同情她们。约瑟芬·巴里小姐本想寄宿在她身边，但比奇伍德离学院太远，根本不可能。于是巴里小姐找到了一个寄宿处，并向马修和玛丽拉保证这就是安妮的住处。 “保管它的女士是一位低级的淑女，”巴里小姐解释道。 “她的丈夫是一名英国军官，她对接收什么样的寄宿生非常谨慎。安妮不会在她的屋檐下遇到任何令人反感的人。桌子很好，房子靠近学院，在一个安静的街区。”

paragraphs.en: “Well,” said Jane with a sigh, “I feel as if I’d lived many moons since the morning. I ought to be home studying my Virgil--that horrid old professor gave us twenty lines to start in on tomorrow. But I simply couldn’t settle down to study tonight. Anne, methinks I see the traces of tears. If you’ve been crying do own up. It will restore my self-respect, for I was shedding tears freely before Ruby came along. I don’t mind being a goose so much if somebody else is goosey, too. Cake? You’ll give me a teeny piece, won’t you? Thank you. It has the real Avonlea flavor.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”简叹了口气说，“我觉得从早上起我已经活了好几个月了。我应该回家学习我的《维吉尔》——那位可怕的老教授给了我们二十行诗，让我们明天开始学习。但我今晚根本无法静下心来学习。安妮，我想我看到了泪水的痕迹。如果你哭过，就承认吧。这会恢复我的自尊，因为在鲁比出现之前我已经在流泪了。我不介意如果别人也有鹅味的话，你就给我一块吧，谢谢，它有真正的埃文利味道。”

chapters.title: Chapter 35: The Winter at Queen's
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 35 章：葵因学院的寒冬拼搏

paragraphs.en: ANNE’S homesickness wore off, greatly helped in the wearing by her weekend visits home. As long as the open weather lasted the Avonlea students went out to Carmody on the new branch railway every Friday night. Diana and several other Avonlea young folks were generally on hand to meet them and they all walked over to Avonlea in a merry party. Anne thought those Friday evening gypsyings over the autumnal hills in the crisp golden air, with the homelights of Avonlea twinkling beyond, were the best and dearest hours in the whole week.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮的思乡之情逐渐消失，周末回家对她的穿着大有帮助。只要天气持续开放，埃文利的学生每周五晚上都会乘坐新的支线铁路前往卡莫迪。戴安娜和其他几个埃文利年轻人通常都会在场迎接他们，他们都在欢乐的聚会中走到埃文利。安妮认为，星期五晚上，吉普赛人在秋天的山丘上，在清新的金色空气中，在远处闪烁着埃文利的家的灯光，是整个星期中最美好的时光。

paragraphs.en: In the Academy Anne gradually drew a little circle of friends about her, thoughtful, imaginative, ambitious students like herself. With the “rose-red” girl, Stella Maynard, and the “dream girl,” Priscilla Grant, she soon became intimate, finding the latter pale spiritual-looking maiden to be full to the brim of mischief and pranks and fun, while the vivid, black-eyed Stella had a heartful of wistful dreams and fancies, as aerial and rainbow-like as Anne’s own.
paragraphs.zh: 在学院里，安妮逐渐建立了一个小朋友圈，这些朋友都是像她一样有思想、富有想象力、雄心勃勃的学生。她很快就与“玫瑰红”女孩斯特拉·梅纳德和“梦中情人”普里西拉·格兰特变得亲密起来，发现后者面色苍白、精神饱满，充满了恶作剧、恶作剧和乐趣，而生动的黑眼睛斯特拉却充满了渴望的梦想和幻想，就像安妮的梦想和幻想一样空中和彩虹。

paragraphs.en: “That Anne-girl improves all the time,” she said. “I get tired of other girls--there is such a provoking and eternal sameness about them. Anne has as many shades as a rainbow and every shade is the prettiest while it lasts. I don’t know that she is as amusing as she was when she was a child, but she makes me love her and I like people who make me love them. It saves me so much trouble in making myself love them.” Then, almost before anybody realized it, spring had come; out in Avonlea the Mayflowers were peeping pinkly out on the sere barrens where snow-wreaths lingered; and the “mist of green” was on the woods and in the valleys. But in Charlottetown harassed Queen’s students thought and talked only of examinations.
paragraphs.zh: “那个安妮女孩一直在进步，”她说。 “我厌倦了其他女孩——她们身上有一种令人发指的、永恒的千篇一律。安妮有彩虹般的多种色调，每一种色调在持续的时候都是最美丽的。我不知道她是否像小时候一样有趣，但她让我爱她，我喜欢那些让我爱她们的人。这让我省去了很多让自己爱她们的麻烦。”然后，几乎在所有人意识到之前，春天已经到来了。在埃文利，五月花号正粉红色地窥视着雪花环徘徊的荒原。 “绿色的薄雾”笼罩在树林和山谷中。但在夏洛特敦，女王学院的学生思想受到困扰，只谈论考试。

paragraphs.en: “I don’t care,” said Josie Pye. “If I don’t pass this year I’m coming back next. My father can afford to send me. Anne, Frank Stockley says that Professor Tremaine said Gilbert Blythe was sure to get the medal and that Emily Clay would likely win the Avery scholarship.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不在乎，”乔西·派伊说。 “如果我今年没通过，我明年就会回来。我父亲可以负担得起送我的费用。安妮，弗兰克·斯托克利说特里梅因教授说吉尔伯特·布莱斯肯定会获得奖牌，艾米丽·克莱很可能会赢得艾弗里奖学金。”

chapters.title: Chapter 36: The Glory and the Dream
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 36 章：荣获奖学金与毕业典礼

paragraphs.en: ON the morning when the final results of all the examinations were to be posted on the bulletin board at Queen’s, Anne and Jane walked down the street together. Jane was smiling and happy; examinations were over and she was comfortably sure she had made a pass at least; further considerations troubled Jane not at all; she had no soaring ambitions and consequently was not affected with the unrest attendant thereon. For we pay a price for everything we get or take in this world; and although ambitions are well worth having, they are not to be cheaply won, but exact their dues of work and self-denial, anxiety and discouragement. Anne was pale and quiet; in ten more minutes she would know who had won the medal and who the Avery. Beyond those ten minutes there did not seem, just then, to be anything worth being called Time.
paragraphs.zh: 那天早上，当所有考试的最终结果都将公布在女王大学的布告栏上时，安妮和简一起走在街上。简微笑着，很高兴。考试结束了，她确信自己至少通过了考试。进一步的考虑并没有让简感到困扰。她没有远大的野心，因此并没有受到随之而来的动乱的影响。因为我们为在这个世界上得到或拿走的一切付出代价；尽管雄心壮志是值得拥有的，但它们并不是廉价获得的，而是要付出努力、自我否定、焦虑和沮丧的代价。安妮脸色苍白，安静。再过十分钟，她就会知道谁赢得了奖牌，谁是艾弗里。在那十分钟之后，似乎就没有什么值得称为时间的东西了。

paragraphs.en: Matthew and Marilla were there, with eyes and ears for only one student on the platform--a tall girl in pale green, with faintly flushed cheeks and starry eyes, who read the best essay and was pointed out and whispered about as the Avery winner. “Reckon you’re glad we kept her, Marilla?” whispered Matthew, speaking for the first time since he had entered the hall, when Anne had finished her essay. “It’s not the first time I’ve been glad,” retorted Marilla. “You do like to rub things in, Matthew Cuthbert.” Miss Barry, who was sitting behind them, leaned forward and poked Marilla in the back with her parasol.
paragraphs.zh: 马修和玛丽拉也在场，他们的眼睛和耳朵只关注着讲台上的一个学生——一个穿淡绿色衣服的高个子女孩，脸颊微微泛红，眼睛闪闪发亮，她读了最好的论文，被指出并低声说她是艾弗里奖得主。 “你认为我们留住了她你很高兴吗，玛丽拉？”当安妮写完论文时，马修低声说道，这是他进入大厅以来第一次说话。 “这不是我第一次感到高兴了，”玛丽拉反驳道。 “你确实喜欢反复强调，马修·库斯伯特。”坐在他们后面的巴里小姐倾身向前，用阳伞戳了戳玛丽拉的后背。

paragraphs.en: “You’ve done splendidly, Anne. I suppose you won’t be teaching now that you’ve won the Avery?” “No. I’m going to Redmond in September. Doesn’t it seem wonderful? I’ll have a brand new stock of ambition laid in by that time after three glorious, golden months of vacation. Jane and Ruby are going to teach. Isn’t it splendid to think we all got through even to Moody Spurgeon and Josie Pye?” “The Newbridge trustees have offered Jane their school already,” said Diana. “Gilbert Blythe is going to teach, too. He has to. His father can’t afford to send him to college next year, after all, so he means to earn his own way through. I expect he’ll get the school here if Miss Ames decides to leave.”
paragraphs.zh: “你做得非常好，安妮。我想你赢得了艾弗里奖后就不会再教书了吧？” “不。我九月要去雷德蒙德。这不是很美妙吗？在度过了三个光辉灿烂的黄金假期后，到那时我就会怀揣着全新的雄心壮志。简和鲁比要教书。想到我们都通过了穆迪·斯布金和乔西·派伊的考验，这不是很棒吗？” “新桥的受托人已经向简提供了他们的学校，”戴安娜说。 “吉尔伯特·布莱斯也要教书。他必须这么做。毕竟，他父亲明年无力供他上大学，所以他打算自己挣钱上大学。如果艾姆斯小姐决定离开，我希望他能在这里上学。”

paragraphs.en: “That is what Rachel said. She was up here one day last week and said there was some talk about it. Matthew felt real worried. All we have saved is in that bank--every penny. I wanted Matthew to put it in the Savings Bank in the first place, but old Mr. Abbey was a great friend of father’s and he’d always banked with him. Matthew said any bank with him at the head of it was good enough for anybody.” “I think he has only been its nominal head for many years,” said Anne. “He is a very old man; his nephews are really at the head of the institution.”
paragraphs.zh: “雷切尔就是这么说的。上周她来过这里，说有人在谈论这件事。马修感到非常担心。我们所有的钱都存进了银行——每一分钱。我一开始就想让马修把钱存进储蓄银行，但老阿比先生是父亲的好朋友，他总是在他的银行里存钱。马修说任何有他领导的银行对任何人来说都足够好了。” “我认为多年来他只是名义上的负责人，”安妮说。 “他是个很老的人了；他的侄子们确实是这个机构的领导者。”

chapters.title: Chapter 37: The Reaper Whose Name is Death
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 37 章：马修去世与绿山墙的哀伤

paragraphs.en: It was Marilla who spoke, alarm in every jerky word. Anne came through the hall, her hands full of white narcissus,--it was long before Anne could love the sight or odor of white narcissus again,--in time to hear her and to see Matthew standing in the porch doorway, a folded paper in his hand, and his face strangely drawn and gray. Anne dropped her flowers and sprang across the kitchen to him at the same moment as Marilla. They were both too late; before they could reach him Matthew had fallen across the threshold. “He’s fainted,” gasped Marilla. “Anne, run for Martin--quick, quick! He’s at the barn.”
paragraphs.zh: 说话的是玛丽拉，每一个生涩的词都充满了惊慌。安妮穿过大厅，手里捧满了白水仙花——过了很久，安妮才再次喜欢上了白水仙花的景象或气味——及时听到了她的声音，看到马修站在门廊门口，手里拿着一张折叠起来的纸，脸色奇怪地憔悴而灰暗。安妮丢下手中的花，和玛丽拉同时穿过厨房跳到他身边。他们都来得太晚了。他们还没来得及找到马修，马修就摔倒在门槛上了。 “他晕倒了，”玛丽拉喘着气说。 “安妮，去找马丁——快点，快点！他在谷仓里。”

paragraphs.en: The news spread quickly through Avonlea, and all day friends and neighbors thronged Green Gables and came and went on errands of kindness for the dead and living. For the first time shy, quiet Matthew Cuthbert was a person of central importance; the white majesty of death had fallen on him and set him apart as one crowned.
paragraphs.zh: 这个消息很快就传遍了埃文利，一整天朋友和邻居都聚集在绿山墙，来来去去为死者和生者提供善意。害羞、安静的马修·库斯伯特第一次成为一个重要人物。死亡的白色威严降临在他身上，使他成为一位加冕者。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, just let me cry, Marilla,” sobbed Anne. “The tears don’t hurt me like that ache did. Stay here for a little while with me and keep your arm round me--so. I couldn’t have Diana stay, she’s good and kind and sweet--but it’s not her sorrow--she’s outside of it and she couldn’t come close enough to my heart to help me. It’s our sorrow--yours and mine. Oh, Marilla, what will we do without him?”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，让我哭吧，玛丽拉，”安妮抽泣着。 “眼泪不会像那种疼痛那样伤害我。在这儿陪我一会儿，用你的手臂搂住我——所以。我不能让戴安娜留下来，她善良、善良、可爱——但这不是她的悲伤——她在悲伤之外，她无法靠近我的心来帮助我。这是我们的悲伤——你的和我的。哦，玛丽拉，没有他我们该怎么办？”

paragraphs.en: “I shall be all right. Diana will come over for company for me. I shall attend to the ironing and baking beautifully--you needn’t fear that I’ll starch the handkerchiefs or flavor the cake with liniment.” “What a girl you were for making mistakes in them days, Anne. You were always getting into scrapes. I did use to think you were possessed. Do you mind the time you dyed your hair?”
paragraphs.zh: “我不会有事的。戴安娜会过来陪我。我会负责熨烫和烘烤得漂亮——你不用担心我会给手帕上浆，或者给蛋糕上搽剂。” “安妮，你在那些日子里真是个容易犯错误的女孩。你总是陷入困境。我以前确实认为你被附身了。你介意你染头发的时间吗？”

chapters.title: Chapter 38: The Bend in the Road
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 38 章：人生的转折点与吉尔伯特的让步（全本终极结局）

paragraphs.en: MARILLA went to town the next day and returned in the evening. Anne had gone over to Orchard Slope with Diana and came back to find Marilla in the kitchen, sitting by the table with her head leaning on her hand. Something in her dejected attitude struck a chill to Anne’s heart. She had never seen Marilla sit limply inert like that. “Yes--no--I don’t know,” said Marilla wearily, looking up. “I suppose I am tired but I haven’t thought about it. It’s not that.” “Did you see the oculist? What did he say?” asked Anne anxiously.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉第二天进城，晚上回来。安妮和戴安娜一起去了果园坡，回来时发现玛丽拉在厨房里，坐在桌边，头靠在手上。她那沮丧的态度让安妮心里感到一阵寒意。她从来没有见过玛丽拉像这样毫无生气地坐着。 “是的——不——我不知道，”玛丽拉抬起头，疲倦地说。 “我想我累了，但我还没有想过。不是那样的。” “你看到眼科医生了吗？他说什么了？”安妮焦急地问道。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Anne, I wish I didn’t have to. But you can see for yourself. I can’t stay here alone. I’d go crazy with trouble and loneliness. And my sight would go--I know it would.” “You won’t have to stay here alone, Marilla. I’ll be with you. I’m not going to Redmond.” “Not going to Redmond!” Marilla lifted her worn face from her hands and looked at Anne. “Why, what do you mean?”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，安妮，我希望我不必这样做。但你可以亲眼看看。我不能独自待在这里。我会因为麻烦和孤独而发疯。我的视力会消失——我知道它会的。” “你不必独自留在这里，玛丽拉。我会和你在一起。我不会去雷德蒙德。” “不去雷德蒙德！”玛丽拉抬起她那张憔悴的脸，看着安妮。 “为什么，你什么意思？”

paragraphs.en: “But I’m going to study Latin and Greek just the same, Mrs. Lynde,” said Anne laughing. “I’m going to take my Arts course right here at Green Gables, and study everything that I would at college.” “Not a bit of it. I shall thrive on it. Oh, I’m not going to overdo things. As ‘Josiah Allen’s wife,’ says, I shall be ‘mejum’. But I’ll have lots of spare time in the long winter evenings, and I’ve no vocation for fancy work. I’m going to teach over at Carmody, you know.” “I don’t know it. I guess you’re going to teach right here in Avonlea. The trustees have decided to give you the school.”
paragraphs.zh: “但我还是要学习拉丁语和希腊语，林德夫人，”安妮笑着说。 “我将在绿山墙学院学习艺术课程，并学习我在大学学习的所有内容。” “一点也不。我会靠它茁壮成长。哦，我不会做得太过分。正如‘约赛亚·艾伦的妻子’所说，我会成为‘mejum’。但在漫长的冬夜里我会有很多空闲时间，而且我没有兴趣从事花哨的工作。你知道，我要去卡莫迪教书。” “我不知道。我猜你会在埃文利教书。董事会决定把学校交给你。”

paragraphs.en: Anne went to the little Avonlea graveyard the next evening to put fresh flowers on Matthew’s grave and water the Scotch rosebush. She lingered there until dusk, liking the peace and calm of the little place, with its poplars whose rustle was like low, friendly speech, and its whispering grasses growing at will among the graves. When she finally left it and walked down the long hill that sloped to the Lake of Shining Waters it was past sunset and all Avonlea lay before her in a dreamlike afterlight--“a haunt of ancient peace.” There was a freshness in the air as of a wind that had blown over honey-sweet fields of clover. Home lights twinkled out here and there among the homestead trees. Beyond lay the sea, misty and purple, with its haunting, unceasing murmur. The west was a glory of soft mingled hues, and the pond reflected them all in still softer shadings. The beauty of it all thrilled Anne’s heart, and she gratefully opened the gates of her soul to it.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，安妮去了埃文利的小墓地，在马修的坟墓上放了鲜花，并给苏格兰玫瑰丛浇水。她在那里逗留到了黄昏，喜欢这个小地方的安宁与平静，白杨树的沙沙声就像低沉而友好的谈话，坟墓间随意生长着低语的小草。当她最终离开这里，走下通往闪亮水域湖的长山时，日落已过，整个埃文利都在梦幻般的余光中展现在她面前——“古老和平的出没之地”。空气中弥漫着一股清新的气息，就像一阵风吹过甜甜的三叶草田一样。家园的树木间到处闪烁着家中的灯光。远处是大海，雾蒙蒙的，紫色的，伴随着令人难以忘怀的、不断的低语声。西方是一片柔和的混合色调的光辉，池塘以更柔和的阴影反射着它们。这一切的美丽震撼了安妮的心，她感激地向这一切打开了自己的灵魂之门。
